title: Fix batches claim race: concurrent first claims raise 23505 on batches_pkey
description:
crates/maverick-store/tests/batches.rs concurrent_claimers_leave_exactly_one_lease_holder fails in about 2 of 3 runs on main (75b6679). claim_batch returns: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "batches_pkey" (23505), Key (id)=(bat_nightly_2026-09-28) already exists.

Cause: crates/maverick-store/src/batches.rs inserts with 'on conflict (kind, batch_window) do nothing'. That names one arbiter index. The id is deterministic from (kind, batch_window), so a concurrent insert of the same row can hit the primary key first, and Postgres raises the PK violation instead of doing nothing.

Fix direction: 'on conflict do nothing' with no arbiter (both unique constraints describe the same row), or treat 23505 as the lost race and fall through to the existing-lease path. Then rerun the test in a loop (for example 20 times) to show it is stable. Found while gating model-maverick-rust-port-3hk.4.7.
close_reason: Fixed: claim_batch insert uses 'on conflict do nothing' with no arbiter, so a concurrent first claim that collides on batches_pkey (deterministic id) is absorbed and falls through to the FOR UPDATE path. Reproduced before the fix: 3/10 runs of concurrent_claimers_leave_exactly_one_lease_holder failed with 23505 on batches_pkey; after: 0/20 runs of the full batches suite failed. .sqlx entry for the changed query replaced.

title: Redact credentials in MAVERICK_SMTP_URL from Config Debug output (G5)
description:
# What
`maverick-config`'s `impl Debug for Config` prints `smtp_url` verbatim (crates/maverick-config/src/lib.rs, the `.field("smtp_url", &self.smtp_url)` line). The URL format is `smtp://[user:pass@]host[:port]/?from=..&to=..` (reference Part 3 §4.3), so it can carry the SMTP password. `alerts_webhook_secret` is already redacted; the SMTP password is not.

# Why
G5 / spec §14.3: credentials never appear in a log line or span. Any `tracing::debug!(?config)` or panic message with the config would leak it.

# Fix
Print the URL with the userinfo password replaced (for example `smtp://user:<redacted>@host:587/?from=..&to=..`), or print only `<set>`/`<unset>`. Add a unit test that the Debug string of a config with `smtp://u:hunter2@h/?from=a@x&to=b@x` does not contain `hunter2`.

Found by CrimsonCarp while wiring alert delivery (bead 3hk.7.11).

title: Get GitHub Actions CI green on main (fast and mutants tiers)
description:
Every push to main has failed CI since the CI gates landed (bf2de20). Root cause of the failures so far: the cargo cache restores ~/.cargo/bin without cargo's install metadata, so 'cargo install' died with 'binary already exists in destination' in the fast and mutants jobs, before any check ran. Commit d1e1eee made the install steps idempotent (skip when the pinned version is present, else --force).

Because of that, the fast tier (fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, cargo deny, sqlx check) and the mutants tier have NEVER run on CI. Local runs of scripts/ci.sh may hide environment differences (installed tools, Docker for testcontainers, sqlx offline data, timeouts).

Work:
1. Check the CI run for d1e1eee or later: 'gh run list --limit 5' and 'gh run view <id> --log-failed'.
2. Fix every real failure in any tier (fast, db, parity, e2e, mutants). Do not weaken a gate to make it pass; if a gate cannot run on GitHub runners, explain why in the commit and ask the owner.
3. Confirm the db, parity, and e2e jobs really run their tests (they finished in about 45s; check they are not empty or skipped).
4. Mutants tier: check its runtime fits the runner; note if it needs sharding.

Done when: a push to main shows all CI jobs green, and the logs show each tier ran its real checks.

title: Port the Model Maverick engine to Rust (engine, trial proxy, conformance harness)
description:
# Goal

Build the Model Maverick engine in Rust so that it gives the same results as the earlier Go engine, except for the approved differences in `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (D1 to D39 as of 2026-09-28; the owner adds rows, agents never do). The engine includes the trial proxy (`crates/maverick-proxy`) and the SDK conformance harness (`crates/sdk-conformance`). Source: `HANDOFF.md`, `plans/master-plan.md` §7.0.

# What the product is (background for every child bead)

Model Maverick (MM) is a B2B recommendation engine for LLMs. It benchmarks model "columns" (provider, model, endpoint, settings) every night against a private task corpus (10 capabilities x 5 difficulty tiers), classifies each incoming workload, applies tenant policy, and returns a ranked list of models (the pick plus a fallback chain). The engine never executes inference for customers. The only MM component that executes inference is the trial proxy, and it uses only the caller's credentials. Four layers: MEASUREMENT (catalog, corpus, runner, graders, scoring, aggregates, calibration), DECISION (classification, policy engine, ranking), ACCOUNTABILITY (prompt hash, decision trace, debug capture, alerts), PLATFORM (tenants + keys, Postgres jobs, the internal seam, MCP, proxy).

# Why this is a port with a complete reference

An earlier Go engine implemented most of v1. Its exact behavior and all 675 of its tests were extracted on 2026-09-28 into:
- `reference/engine-reference.md` (about 4,300 lines, Parts 1 to 7: store/config/CLI, measurement-io, measurement-core, decision, API/MCP, proxy, SQL catalog). Search it; do not read it end to end.
- `parity/` : `fixtures/<area>/` (inputs plus full-precision expected outputs), `manifest/<area>.json` (every Go test mapped to its replacement), `schema/` (migrations, `schema.sql`, 98 sqlc queries), `blackbox/` (619 recorded HTTP exchanges plus 1,498 seed SQL statements), `DIVERGENCES.md`.
The Go source is NOT available and is not needed. Never try to find, run, or rebuild it. Where specs name Go tools (chi, pgx, sqlc, goose, River, `cmd/`, `internal/`), use the Rust stack.

# Owner decisions already made (2026-09-28)
Fresh database; corpus in the private repo `donnfelker/model-maverick-corpus`; hosted plus binary trial proxy; direct execution by default (OpenRouter opt-in); classifier limits 1000/tenant/day and $5/day (placeholders); models.dev price source; M6b commercial gate suspended (the project may be open-sourced); divergences D26 to D39. Remaining owner items are end-of-project only: provider keys and the deploy host.

# Order of authority when documents disagree
1. `specs/` (the engine contract is `specs/model-maverick-v1-spec.md`)
2. `parity/DIVERGENCES.md`
3. `reference/engine-reference.md` (exact strings, constants, order, quirks)
4. `plans/master-plan.md`

# Work packages (children of this epic) and their order
1. Workspace + CI gates. Blocks everything.
2a. Pure domain crates. 2b. Schema, store, config, CLI. 2c. Provider clients, fake provider, runner. (2a, 2b, 2c run in parallel.)
2d. HTTP API, MCP, internal seam (needs 2a + 2b); trial proxy + maverick-core (needs 2a; replay needs a mock engine).
2e. Jobs on graphile_worker (needs 2a, 2b, 2c).
3. SDK conformance harness (needs maverick-core and the proxy).
4. Port completion: manifest audit, privacy/canary tests, latency checks, deploy, go-live, first live nightly (owner-gated).

# Definition of done for the whole port (HANDOFF §5)
- Every entry in `parity/manifest/*.json` has a passing Rust test, or an approved row in `DIVERGENCES.md`.
- The API replay (`parity/blackbox/`) and the proxy replay (`parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json`) have zero unexplained diffs.
- CI gates pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo deny`, `cargo-mutants` on the domain crates.
- The first live nightly on Rust completes below the spend cap (needs the owner). The owner chose a fresh database (2026-09-28), so there are no Go-vs-Rust distribution checks. The Go implementation was never shipped.

# Rules that apply to every child (from AGENTS.md, guarantees G1 to G14)
- A package is complete only when its Rust tests pass the parity data for its area. Compiling is not enough. No package is done with a diff that is neither fixed nor matched to a DIVERGENCES row. A `QUIRK:` in the reference is Go behavior to reproduce unless DIVERGENCES lists it.
- Do not add a new intended difference yourself. Ask the owner; after approval add a DIVERGENCES row and update the spec.
- Privacy (G5): never store a prompt except in an encrypted debug-capture window; no prompt, completion, request body, or credential in spans, logs, or metric labels; every `#[tracing::instrument]` uses `skip_all` plus an allowlist.
- Zero retention fails closed and outranks G1 and G14.
- Corpus is private (G7): never copy task prompts, golden answers, or rubrics into this repo.
- No real provider calls in CI; use the deterministic fake provider. One opt-in, spend-capped live smoke test only.
- Spend is capped (G8). Pools are hard boundaries (G2). No schema translation. No `POST /v1/outcomes`. No Redis. No MM-owned provider keys for customer traffic.
- Git: plain git, stage by name, one commit per unit of work with the co-author trailer, no push or PR without owner approval.
- Do not compare live benchmark runs for equality (5.37% of model-question pairs flip across identical runs).

title: Package 1: Cargo workspace, crate layout, and CI gates
description:
# Goal
Create the Cargo workspace at the repo root with crates under `crates/`, and make every CI gate from AGENTS.md run and pass on an empty build. This package blocks every other package. Parity gate: CI is green on an empty build (HANDOFF §4 row 1, master plan §6).

# Why first
Every later package needs: a crate to put code in, the shared parity-fixture test helpers, the Postgres testcontainers helper, and CI gates that fail loudly. Setting the gates before code exists stops lint debt from growing (clippy `-D warnings`, the bare-`#[instrument]` lint, `cargo deny` license/advisory policy).

# Required crates (AGENTS.md, plan §4 and §6)
- `maverick-core` : the Rust copy of the shared SDK core (recommend client, chain executor, fail-open ladder, telemetry batcher, alias grammar, workload projection). The proxy depends on it by path.
- `maverick-proxy` : the trial proxy binary (no database, own deployment).
- `sdk-conformance` : mock engine plus mock provider, twelve frozen scenarios.
The agent decides how to divide the engine crates. Guidance: keep pure domain logic (no I/O, no SQL) in crates that `cargo-mutants` can run on quickly; keep the store (sqlx) in its own crate; keep the API (axum) free of business logic (spec §2.2 rule: API has no business logic; recommend and policy contain no SQL; everything reaches Postgres through the store). A split workspace also manages compile times (plan §11 risk).

# Stack (AGENTS.md)
Rust stable, 2024 edition. Tokio, axum + tower, sqlx 0.9 (compile-time checked, offline mode in CI), `graphile_worker` 0.13.x, reqwest + rustls (no OpenSSL anywhere), hand-written provider clients, `jsonschema` (draft 2020-12), serde + a maintained serde YAML crate, `rmcp`, `tracing` JSON + `tracing-opentelemetry` + `opentelemetry-otlp`, RustCrypto (`hmac`, `sha2`, `hkdf`, `aes-gcm`, `subtle`), `ulid`, testcontainers, `insta`.

# Children
Workspace skeleton; CI gate pipeline; instrument lint; parity fixture test-support crate; manifest coverage checker; Postgres testcontainers helper.
close_reason: All 7 children closed. Gate verified 2026-09-29 on a clean copy of HEAD 809c025: scripts/ci.sh fast exit 0 (fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo deny, sqlx prepare --check); instrument lint run directly: 95 files, no violations, self-test rejects the bad fixture.

title: Create the Cargo workspace skeleton and crate layout under crates/
description:
# What
Create the root `Cargo.toml` workspace (resolver 3, edition 2024, `rust-toolchain.toml` pinned to current stable), `[workspace.dependencies]` for the whole stack, `[workspace.lints]` (deny warnings via clippy in CI, `unsafe_code = "forbid"` unless a crate needs it), and empty crates under `crates/` that compile.

# Required crate names (AGENTS.md)
`maverick-core`, `maverick-proxy` (bin), `sdk-conformance` (bin + lib for vectors).

# Suggested engine split (the agent decides; record the final layout in a short `crates/README.md`)
- `maverick-domain` (or several small crates): ids, task/grader types, graders, scoring, EWMA, ranking, policy, ceilings, bands, checks, reasons, predictions math, spend math, catalog lifecycle, capture crypto, fingerprints, key format, classifier pure logic, telemetry derivation. Pure: no tokio I/O, no sqlx. This is what `cargo-mutants` runs on, so keep it fast to build.
- `maverick-store`: sqlx pool, migrations, queries, transactions.
- `maverick-config`: env parsing and validation.
- `maverick-providers`: provider clients, fake provider, retry.
- `maverick-runner`, `maverick-jobs`, `maverick-api` (axum + MCP), `maverick-alerts`.
- `maverick` (bin): CLI entry, wiring (`serve`, `migrate`, `corpus`, `mcp-stdio`, `demo-run`).
- `parity-support` (dev-only): fixture loading helpers (separate bead).
Dependency direction: api -> services -> domain; store is the only crate with SQL; domain depends on nothing I/O-bound.

# Stack pins
tokio, axum, tower, tower-http, sqlx 0.9 (postgres, runtime-tokio, tls-rustls, macros, migrate), graphile_worker 0.13.x (pin exact minor; plan says own a fork if it stalls), reqwest (rustls-tls, no default features), jsonschema, serde, serde_json, a maintained serde YAML crate (not the archived serde_yaml), rmcp, tracing, tracing-subscriber (json), tracing-opentelemetry, opentelemetry-otlp, hmac, sha2, hkdf, aes-gcm, subtle, ulid, rand (CSPRNG via OsRng), testcontainers, insta, proptest.

# Also
- `.gitignore` for `target/`.
- No OpenSSL in the dependency tree (cargo deny will enforce).
- Workspace compiles with `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` (zero tests OK).

# Done when
`cargo build --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. Commit.

title: Set up CI gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, cargo deny, cargo-mutants, sqlx offline
description:
# What
A CI pipeline (GitHub Actions workflow file plus a local `scripts/ci.sh` or `just`/`make` target that runs the same steps, so agents can run CI locally without pushing) with these gates, from AGENTS.md "Tests and quality gates":
1. `cargo fmt --all --check`
2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
3. `cargo test --workspace` (Postgres tests via testcontainers need Docker in CI)
4. `cargo deny check` with a `deny.toml`: license allowlist, advisories, bans (ban `openssl`, `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`), sources (crates.io only unless a pinned git fork of graphile_worker is needed). The owner may open-source the project (2026-09-28): allow only permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, MPL-2.0 as file-level) and deny copyleft (GPL, AGPL, LGPL) so any later open-source license choice stays possible.
5. `cargo mutants` on the domain crates only (slow; a separate job, and run locally before committing a domain unit per plan §6).
6. sqlx offline mode: `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` in CI with the `.sqlx/` query cache committed; `cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace` fails if the cache is stale.
7. The bare-`#[instrument]` lint (bead 1.3).

# Test tiers (the script grows as later beads land)
Structure the script and workflow as named tiers so later beads only register their suite: `fast` (fmt, clippy, unit tests, no Docker), `db` (testcontainers store and job tests), `parity` (manifest coverage checker from bead 1.5 in report mode, later strict; API replay 5.15; proxy replay 6.11; conformance 8.3), `e2e` (full-stack script 9.10; job crash acceptance 7.12), `mutants`. `scripts/ci.sh <tier>` runs one tier; no argument runs all but `mutants`. Every tier writes logs and test reports to `target/ci/<tier>/` and the workflow uploads that directory as an artifact on failure, so a red run can be diagnosed without re-running.

# Rules
- No real provider keys in CI, ever. No network calls to providers. The live smoke test is `#[ignore]` and env-gated.
- The private corpus is never available in CI; corpus tests skip when `MAVERICK_CORPUS_DIR` is unset.
- Do not push or open PRs without owner approval; the workflow file is committed locally.

# Done when
The local CI script runs every tier (empty tiers pass) and is green on the empty workspace. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Add a CI lint that rejects bare #[instrument] (G5 telemetry redaction control)
description:
# What
A CI check that fails if any `#[tracing::instrument]` / `#[instrument]` attribute lacks `skip_all`. Every instrument must use `skip_all` with an explicit allowlist of `fields(...)`. A bare `#[instrument]` records every argument via Debug, which could put a prompt, completion, request body, or credential into a span.

# Why (D19, plan §6, spec §14.3)
Telemetry redaction is a G5 control. Prompt text, completions, request bodies, and credential headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `X-Maverick-API-Key`) are never span attributes, log fields, or metric labels; fingerprints only. The Go engine used slog JSON logs; the Rust engine adds OTel, so this lint is new.

# How
A small script (grep/ripgrep or a tiny Rust xtask using `syn`) over `crates/**/*.rs`. Prefer the syn-based xtask so multi-line attributes are handled. Include a self-test: a fixture file with a bare instrument must fail the check.

# Done when
The lint runs in the CI script, fails on a bare instrument, passes on the workspace. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: crates/instrument-lint (token-based checker: bare, missing skip_all, ret/err, cfg_attr, macro bodies, renamed import) plus scripts/check-instrumentation.sh with a bad-fixture self-test; wired into scripts/ci.sh fast

title: Build the parity-support test crate (fixture loading, float compare, DIVERGENCES helpers)
description:
# What
A dev-only crate used by every package's tests to read `parity/` data consistently.

# Features
- Locate the repo root and load `parity/fixtures/<area>/<file>.json` with anchor support: manifest `where` values look like `fixtures/decision/policy_evaluate.json#section/case-id`. Provide `fixture(area, file)` and `case(anchor)` helpers returning `serde_json::Value` or a typed struct.
- Float helpers: exact f64 compare; compare-at-tolerance (the reference gives 1e-12 for map-order summation); and `as_f32_widened(x)` for values that Postgres stores as `real` (float32) and Go widened to float64. Many expected values (quality bars, pass rates, EWMAs) are float32-widened; the reference marks each one.
- A `divergence!("D6")` marker macro or attribute-style comment convention that a test uses when it asserts the Rust expected column instead of the recorded Go value, so the manifest checker can see it.
- Loading of `parity/fixtures/measurement-io/testdata/**` and `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/**` raw files (YAML tasks, schemas, prompt text) byte for byte.

# Notes
- Data and contracts in parity (SQL, prompts, schemas, error strings, headers, wire bytes) were copied byte for byte. Never normalize whitespace when loading prompt text or wire bytes.
- Remove the stray `.DS_Store` files only if the owner agrees; they are harmless, ignore them in loaders.

# Done when
Helpers exist with their own unit tests and are used by at least one smoke test that loads a fixture from each area. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Build the manifest coverage checker (every Go test has a Rust test or a DIVERGENCES row)
description:
# What
A tool (xtask or test) that reads `parity/manifest/*.json` (api 256 rows, decision 105, measurement-core 173, measurement-io 144, proxy 66, store 92; 675 Go tests total, 640 unique names, subtests listed separately) and reports, for each `go_test` entry, the Rust test that replaces it or the `DIVERGENCES.md` row (D1 to D39 today; read the file, do not hard-code the list) that explains why not. It fails when an entry has neither.

# Why
AGENTS.md parity rule: "Each Go test in `parity/manifest/*.json` must have a Rust test that replaces it, or a DIVERGENCES.md row that explains why not." HANDOFF §5 makes this the first item of the definition of done. Without a mechanical check, coverage drifts silently (plan §11 "port drift" risk).

# Suggested mechanism
A mapping convention the checker can read, for example a doc comment or attribute on each Rust test: `/// parity: decision/policy.TestEvaluatePoolRestriction` (use the exact `go_test` string), or a checked-in `parity/rust-map.toml` generated and maintained per package. The checker greps the workspace for the tags and joins against the manifests. Report per area: covered, divergence-justified, missing. Also flag Rust tags that name a Go test not in any manifest (typos).

# Rollout
Run it in CI in report mode at first (packages are incomplete), and make each package's closing bead require zero missing entries for its area. The final completion bead turns it to strict mode.

# Done when
The checker runs locally, prints per-area coverage, and has a strict flag. Commit.
close_reason: Built parity-coverage manifest checker (bin in parity-support): parses parity/manifest/*.json, scans crates for 'parity:' tags, matches DIVERGENCES rows; per-area report + --strict; 13 tests; detects 12 existing tags and D37 on real data

title: Build the Postgres testcontainers helper for store and job tests
description:
# What
A shared test helper that starts Postgres 16 (image `postgres:16-alpine`, matching the Go suite) with testcontainers, runs the engine migrations, and hands out isolated databases per test (create database from a migrated template for speed, or a schema per test). Support an env override (for example `MAVERICK_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) to use an existing server, mirroring how the Go recording used `API_TEST_DATABASE_URL` when Docker was unavailable.

# Why
AGENTS.md: store tests and job tests use real Postgres (testcontainers), never mocks. The API replay also needs one real database. Float32 `real` storage, `timestamptz` behavior, and transaction semantics only match on real Postgres.

# Notes
- Migration runner comes from package 2b; until it exists, the helper can accept a migration closure. Wire the real migrations when 2b lands.
- Keep container startup to once per test binary (a `OnceCell` / `LazyLock`).
- The job acceptance tests need to kill and restart workers against the same database; expose the connection URL, not only a pool.

# Done when
A sample test creates a database, runs a trivial query, and tears down; works with Docker and with the env override. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: crates/maverick-testdb. One postgres:16-alpine container per test binary (Go storetest parity: db/user/password maverick, ready line x2, 2 min timeout), Schema (empty/sql/sqlx migrator/custom, chainable) applied once to a hashed template db, one cloned db per test, dropped on close/Drop. MAVERICK_TEST_DATABASE_URL override verified; Go skip line without Docker; CI/MAVERICK_TEST_REQUIRE_DB turns skip into failure; orphaned containers reaped by label+pid. Package 2b wires Schema::sqlx(&MIGRATOR).then(graphile_worker schema) when the migrations land.

title: Build shared test observability: per-test log capture, step logger, parity diff reporters, secret-leak check
description:
# What
Shared test observability so every failing test explains itself: a per-test tracing subscriber, a step logger for multi-step tests, and readable diffs for parity comparisons. Every package uses it. Polish-round requirement: "comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging."

# Features (in the parity-support dev crate or a sibling `test-support` crate)
- `init_test_tracing()`: installs a per-test `tracing` subscriber (for example via `tracing-test` or a custom capture layer) that records all engine log lines and spans at DEBUG, prints them only when the test fails, and honors `RUST_LOG` to narrow noise. Output format matches the engine's JSON log shape so production logs and test logs read the same.
- A redaction check in the capture layer: if a captured line contains a registered secret (test API keys, master keys, canary strings), fail the test. This makes every test a small G5 check for free.
- `step!("...")` macro/helper for multi-step tests (store tests, replay, e2e, acceptance): logs a numbered step with elapsed time, so a failure shows the last completed step.
- Parity diff helpers: for JSON, a field-path diff (`$.recommendations[1].score: expected 94.1, got 94.2`) with the fixture anchor (`fixtures/decision/rank.json#case-7`) and any D-row tag in the message; for bytes (wire bodies, SSE, rewritten bodies), a hex+text diff around the first mismatch; for floats, show both values in full precision and as f32 bits.
- Replay reporter: a summary table at the end of a replay run (total, passed, allowlisted by D-row, unexplained), plus one detailed block per unexplained diff with request, expected response, actual response.
- Conventions doc (`crates/test-support/README.md`): name tests with the parity tag, one assertion message per fixture case, never log prompt/corpus content.

# Done when
Helpers exist with their own tests, and at least one test per helper demonstrates the failure output. Commit.
close_reason: Built test-support crate: per-test tracing capture, G5 secret-leak guard, step! logging, JSON/bytes/float diff reporters, replay reporter; 21 tests green; fmt+clippy+workspace CI fast pass

Collect every item that only the owner can supply or decide (HANDOFF §6 and §7, AGENTS.md "When to stop and ask the owner", master plan §10). Each child is a `question` bead. title: OWNER: grant access to the private corpus repo (modelmaverick-corpus)
description:
# What is needed
Read access to the private corpus repository `modelmaverick-corpus` (about 220 authored tasks: task YAML per capability plus authoring notes), checked out OUTSIDE this directory.

# What it unblocks
- Loading a real corpus version (`maverick corpus load`, `corpus activate`) against a real database.
- The two jobs tests that need the private corpus (reference Part 3 §6; parity/README "Known gaps": they exist only as given/when/then cases).
- Real benchmarks and the first live Rust nightly.

# Hard rules (G7, AGENTS.md)
Never copy corpus content (task prompts, golden answers, rubrics, grader internals) into this directory, into any public artifact, into logs, or into a benchmarked model's prompt beyond the task prompt. Corpus-dependent tests gate on a corpus checkout path supplied by env var and skip cleanly when it is absent. The small mini-corpora in `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/e2e_corpus/` are synthetic test data and are fine to use.

# Close when
The owner has granted access and told us the checkout location convention (env var name for tests).

title: OWNER: approve DIVERGENCES rows for proxy behaviors the plan requires but D1-D25 do not list
description:
# The gap
`reference/engine-reference.md` Part 6 §11, §13, §16, §17 lists proxy behaviors the master plan requires but that have NO row in `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (D1 to D25). AGENTS.md: "Do not add a new intended difference yourself. Ask the owner. After approval, add a row to DIVERGENCES.md and update the spec." The proxy replay (`parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json`) will show diffs for these, and without rows they count as bugs.

# Items needing a decision (each: approve a new D-row, or keep Go behavior)
1. Retry-After: Go ignores it (QUIRK 11: a 429 advances immediately). Plan §3.5 core: "respect Retry-After". Scenario `x_chat_429_advances`.
2. Telemetry batching: Go sends one batch per request, from a detached goroutine, no exit flush. Plan §3.5 core batcher: 10 s / 20 items / exit flush, per tenant key.
3. Proxy rate limits: Go has none. Plan §3.5: "tighter rate limits than the API", per tenant key.
4. Parameter normalization: Go has exactly two mappings (chat `reasoning_effort` xhigh -> high; messages `output_config.effort` xhigh -> max). Plan §3.5: "normalized to the nearest value the routed model accepts", catalog-driven.

7. Any Go QUIRK in Part 6 §16 that the maverick-core chain executor would naturally change (for example QUIRK 9, mid-stream abort relayed as a clean end; QUIRK 12, a 502 written to a gone client).

# Agent guidance until answered
Build the proxy so each item is a small, isolated switch, and run the replay against Go behavior first. Do not ship the Rust behavior for an item without a row. The owner may approve all of them in one pass.

# Close when
The owner has decided each item, and approved rows are added to DIVERGENCES.md and the spec.

# The question
The OpenRouter execution spec uses `provider.zdr` as the per-request Zero Data Retention option. Nobody has confirmed that name against the OpenRouter API (HANDOFF §7).

D15: for a zero-retention tenant, openrouter-mode executors (SDK core and hosted proxy) send OpenRouter's per-request ZDR option on every attempt and skip any alias not verified `zero`; if nothing remains the result is `409 no_compliant_columns`. A wrong parameter name silently sends zero-retention traffic without the protection. This is a privacy guarantee, so it fails closed.

Keep the parameter name in one constant, cite this bead in a comment, and do not ship openrouter-mode for zero-retention tenants to production until confirmed.

title: Package 2a: Pure domain crates (ids, tasks, graders, scoring, ranking, policy, ceilings, alias, crypto)
description:
# Goal
Port every pure (no I/O, no SQL) piece of engine logic into domain crates, gated by the fixture files in `parity/fixtures/`. HANDOFF §4 row 2a; master plan §7.0 step 2(a). Reference Parts 2, 3, 4.

# Scope
IDs (prefix + ULID), task and grader types (serde tagged enums), the corpus file loader and validator, the grader framework and the five grader kinds (JSON schema, rule scan, golden answer, key facts, judge rubric; test_suite is reserved and rejected), scoring (run quality, high-stakes overlay, variance and ambiguity penalties, judge order swap, cell observation, availability, censored latency), EWMA + Welford, regression detection math, prediction/Brier/overconfidence math, spend projection math, ranking (modes, bands, noise band, same-family tie bias, availability floor), ceilings and banded policy, policy engine (pool, allowlist, standing constraints incl. zero retention, request preferences, G4 simulation/validation), check specs and reasons, alias grammar, workload projection, capture crypto and fingerprints, API key format and hashing, classifier pure logic (prompt text, parse, truncation, degraded tracker), telemetry outcome derivation, catalog lifecycle logic.

# Why a separate package
These are the numbers the product sells. They must match Go bit-for-bit where fixtures demand it (float32 storage widening, map-order summation at 1e-12), and `cargo-mutants` must run on them. Keeping them pure makes that fast and lets 2a run in parallel with 2b and 2c.

# Parity rules for every child
- Write the Rust tests from the fixture file first, then the code.
- Each Go test named in `parity/manifest/<area>.json` for the child's area needs a Rust test that replaces it (or a DIVERGENCES row). Name the Rust test so the manifest checker can map it.
- Before asserting, read `parity/DIVERGENCES.md`. If a row applies (D1, D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D14, D16, D18, D24, D29, D36 touch this package), assert the Rust expected column, not the recorded Go value.
- Go regex `\d \w \s \b` are ASCII-only and Go lowercases per rune. Use `(?-u:\w)` style ASCII classes and per-char lowercasing where fixtures need Go results (reference Part 2 §15).
- Postgres `real` columns are float32; many expected values are float32 widened to float64. The reference marks each one.
- Six property tests used Go's RNG; implement them as properties (proptest or similar), not as replayed streams.
- Serde enums for tagged unions: an unknown variant fails at deserialization; a missing match arm fails at compile time.

# Done when
All child beads closed, all `parity/fixtures/{decision,measurement-io,measurement-core}` pure fixtures pass, `cargo-mutants` runs clean (or survivors are justified) on the domain crates, clippy clean.

title: Port the variance penalty, ambiguity penalty, and judge order-swap folding
description:
# What
The variance penalty over repeats, the ambiguity penalty over shared dimensions, and the judge order-swap folding. Spec §6.2, §6.3; reference Part 3 §1.

# Formulas
Variance (over repeats that produced gradable output; runner.repeats = 3):
- `mu = mean(q_run)`, `sigma = stddev(q_run)` (sigma = 0 when only one gradable repeat; check the reference for population vs sample stddev and match Go).
- `task_score = max(0, mu - lambda_var * sigma)`, `lambda_var = 0.5` (config `MAVERICK_SCORING_LAMBDA_VAR`).
- Missing repeats (errors, timeouts) do not enter mu but are recorded. A pair with zero gradable repeats contributes no task score and counts against availability (D6).

Ambiguity:
- When two or more graders score the same output on the same task dimension (via `weight_dimensions`), `a_output = stddev(scores for the shared dimension on this output)`; `a = mean(a_output over repeats)`.
- `task_score = max(0, task_score - lambda_amb * a)`, `lambda_amb = 0.25` (config `MAVERICK_SCORING_LAMBDA_AMB`).
- Judge order-swap disagreement is folded into `a_output` as two observations of the judge's dimension.
- Cells also aggregate `a` as the `ambiguity` dimension.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/penalties.json` (12 rows) and `orderswap.json` (9 rows).

# Done when
All rows pass at the reference's stated tolerance. Mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: scoring::penalties (variance_penalty, shared_dimension_spread, ambiguity, ambiguity_penalty, order_swap_observations, grader_observations folding). All 21 penalties/orderswap rows + extras tagged; 0 missed mutants.

title: Port cell observation, EWMA + Welford fold, availability (D6), censored latency (D7), measured flag
description:
# What
Cell observation per batch, the new availability dimension, censored latency percentiles, the EWMA fold with Welford variance, and the `measured` flag. Spec §6.4; reference Part 3 §1. The DB-backed `aggregate_rebuild` job that calls this is in package 2e.

# Formulas
- Cell = (column, capability, difficulty tier). Observation `x_t(cell) = mean(task_score over the cell's tasks in this batch)`.
- Dimensions per cell per batch: `quality` (gradable runs only; stored in [0,1], displayed x100 with one decimal), `pass_rate` (fraction of task-repeats passing; errors and timeouts count as failures), `ambiguity`, `latency_p50_ms`, `latency_p95_ms`, `cost_per_run_usd` (mean), `availability` (NEW).
- EWMA per (cell, dimension), seeded by the first observation: `S_0 = x_0`; `S_t = alpha * x_t + (1 - alpha) * S_{t-1}`, alpha = 0.3 (`MAVERICK_SCORING_ALPHA`).
- `aggregates.variance` is the running Welford variance of the x_t series (used by regression scan). `n` counts observations. `measured = (n >= scoring.min_nights)`, default 3 (`MAVERICK_SCORING_MIN_NIGHTS`). The plan phrases this as "3 distinct nights"; confirm with the reference whether n counts nights or observations and match Go.
- Smoke and sweep observations feed the same EWMA stream.

# Divergences
- D6: new per-cell `availability` = fraction of every scheduled repeat in the cell (including timeouts and provider errors) that returned output. Go has no such dimension.
- D7: latency percentiles include each timeout, censored at the timeout value. Go folded latency only from runs with a measured latency. Assert the Rust rule and tag D7 where a Go fixture differs.

# Float32 (critical for parity)
Postgres stores `real` as float32. The Go fold read float32 values, computed in float64, and stored float32. Fixtures are "bit-exact under float32 storage" (plan §7.0 step 2(e)). Reproduce the same widen/narrow points exactly; the reference marks each value.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/observe.json` (4 rows) and `ewma.json` (5 rows). Property: EWMA convergence (spec §15), written as a property test.

# Done when
All rows pass bit-exact where required. Mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: scoring::observe (Observe, nearest-rank percentile, D6 availability, D7 censored timeouts via RunStats::from_run) and scoring::ewma (Stream fold/resume/variance/measured, fold_observation bit-exact through f32 storage). 9 observe/ewma rows + extras tagged; EWMA convergence proptest; 0 missed mutants.

title: Port regression-detection math and the parse-failure watch
description:
# What
The pure math of regression detection and the parse-failure watch. The `regression_scan` job that reads aggregates and writes alerts is in package 2e. Spec §6.5, §11; reference Part 3 §1 and §2.

# Rules
- Smoothed drop: `S_t < max(S over trailing 7 days) - 3.0` (quality points on the 0 to 100 scale).
- Raw shock: `x_t < S_{t-1} - max(2 * sqrt(variance), 3.0)`.
- Severity: warning; critical if the cell's column is in any tenant pool AND the drop crosses that tenant's quality bar.
- Dedupe: one alert per cell per 7 days unless the drop deepens by >= 2 further points (re-arm).
- Parse-failure watch: a column's batch parse-failure rate > 5% AND > 2x its trailing 7-day rate raises `parse_failure_rate` (the leading indicator of caller-side silent escalation).

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/regression.json` (8 rows). Given/when/then cases that need DB state are in reference Part 3 §6 and belong to the regression_scan job bead.

# Done when
All rows pass. Mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port the G8 spend projection math
description:
# What
The pure spend projection used by the G8 spend guard. The guard's job wiring (refusal, alerts, skipped batch) is in package 2e. Spec §11 "Spend guard"; reference Part 3 §2; master plan §3.1.

# Formula
`projected = sum over (task x column x repeats) of (input_tokens_est(task) * p_in + task.max_tokens * p_out)`, with `input_tokens_est = ceil(chars(prompt + attachments) / 4) + 600`. The reference (exact Go behavior) wins; follow it and note it in the test.

- "chars" means what Go counted (bytes or runes). Check the reference and match it.

title: Port request-time policy evaluation (pool, allowlist, standing constraints, preferences) with D1 zero retention
description:
# What
Request-time policy evaluation: the fixed five-step order that turns a pool into ranked survivors, recording every exclusion with a closed-enum reason. Spec §7.1, §7.3, §7.5; reference Part 4 §1 "policy" (exact error strings, order, reason spellings).

# Order of operations
1. Pool restriction (G2). `request.pool` by name, else the tenant's default. Unknown pool -> `422 unknown_pool`. Candidates = pool columns minus retired. A request can narrow a pool; it can never widen it.
2. Allowlist (G3). Each `allowed_models` entry resolves against the SYSTEM catalog. No match -> `422 unknown_model` naming the entry. Resolves but not in pool -> `422 model_not_in_pool` naming the entry. title: Port the ranking algorithm (modes, bands, noise-band ties, D8 availability floor, D9 entry fields)
description:
# What
The ranking algorithm over policy survivors, producing the pick (index 0) and the pool-constrained fallback chain. Spec §7.4; reference Part 4 §2 "recommend" (exact tie-break order, float handling, reason strings).

# Algorithm
Inputs per candidate: Q = quality EWMA x100, P = pass_rate EWMA, C = cost_per_run_usd EWMA, L = latency_p95_ms EWMA, A = mean availability over the trailing 7 nights, measured. Quality/pass come from `quality_source_column_id` when set (secondary endpoints borrow quality from their primary; latency and cost stay their own).
- Normalize over survivors only, per query, never stored: `nQ = minmax(Q)`, `nC = 1 - minmax(C)`, `nL = 1 - minmax(L)`. minmax over one survivor or equal values yields 1.0 for all.
- `V = w_q*nQ + w_c*nC + w_l*nL`. Default weights when the tenant has no `tenant_weights` row for the capability: quality 0.8/0.1/0.1, balanced 0.5/0.35/0.15, cost 0.25/0.6/0.15.
1. Band by mode: quality 0.0, balanced 1.5, cost 5.5 quality points (`MAVERICK_RANKING_BAND_*`). Leaders = `Q >= max(Q) - band`, within the preference-satisfying partition first.
2. Order leaders by V descending.
3. Append non-leaders by Q descending (the tail is a sane escalation chain).
4. Noise-band ties: adjacent candidates with `|Qi - Qj| <= 0.75` (`MAVERICK_RANKING_NOISE_BAND`) reorder cheaper C first; prefer a same-family (same provider) cheaper downgrade over a cross-family swap.
5. Preference violators sort after all satisfiers, ordered by the same rules.
6. D8 (new): candidates with A below the availability floor (default 0.9, `MAVERICK_RANKING_AVAILABILITY_FLOOR`) rank after every candidate at or above it, ordered by the same rules, and carry `low_availability: true`. Go had no availability input.

# Entry fields (D9)
Every chain entry carries its column's `settings` (reasoning effort, thinking mode) and its effective `retention_mode`, plus `low_availability`. Displayed `score` is absolute quality x100 with one decimal (`rank_extras.json` display_score); ranking normalization is never shown.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/rank.json` (4 rows), `rank_extras.json` (1 row: display_score, high_stakes), `rank_property.json` (3 property rows; implement as properties: normalization bounds, etc.). New tests for D8 ordering. Where Go fixtures lack `settings`/`retention_mode`/`low_availability`, assert the Rust shape and tag D8/D9.

# Done when
All rows pass, D8 tests added, mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port the alias grammar into maverick-core (with D14 ?settings=caller)
description:
# What
The alias grammar, parsed identically everywhere (proxy, SDK cores, engine). Lives in `maverick-core` so the proxy and the conformance harness share one implementation. Reference Part 6 §5 (`ParseAlias`); master plan §3.5; spec §7.4 (settings opt-out).

# Go grammar (reproduce exactly)
Input: the raw `model` string. Output `{pool, mode}` or one of two errors.
1. Must start with the exact, case-sensitive prefix `maverick/`, else `not_maverick_alias`.
2. `rest` = everything after the prefix.
3. If `rest` contains `:`, split at the FIRST `:` into pool and modeWord; either part empty -> `malformed_alias`. Else pool = "" and modeWord = rest.
4. modeWord (exact, case-sensitive): `auto` -> balanced, `quality` -> quality, `cost` -> cost. Anything else (including `balanced`, `AUTO`, "", " auto") -> `malformed_alias`.
Consequences: pool is any non-empty string without `:` (spaces and `/` allowed, no trimming). `maverick/prod:pool:auto` is malformed. `maverick/auto:auto` is pool `auto`, mode balanced. Both error kinds map to the same HTTP 400 in the proxy.

# Divergence D14 (settings opt-out)
Rust adds the suffix `?settings=caller`, for example `maverick/<pool>:<mode>?settings=caller` (and presumably `maverick/auto?settings=caller`). Default: the proxy and SDK cores apply the recommended entry's `settings`; with the suffix they leave the caller's settings alone. In Go this string is `malformed_alias` (400). Tag the affected unit.json rows D14 and assert the Rust result. Keep the parse output struct explicit: `{pool: Option, mode, settings_mode: Apply|Caller}`.

# Other rule
A concrete model name where an alias is expected is rejected by the proxy (400) and passed through untouched by an SDK ("don't route, just call it"). The parser returns `not_maverick_alias`; the caller decides.

title: Define and implement the versioned workload projection in maverick-core (D5)
description:
# What
The versioned workload projection (D5): one definition, shared by the proxy and every SDK core, that turns a chat request (OpenAI chat completions or Anthropic Messages) into the prompt text the classifier sees. Lives in `maverick-core`. Spec v1 §8.1 "Workload projection"; `plans/model-maverick-sdk-v0-plan.md` §2.1; master plan §3.5; reference Part 6 §6 (the Go rule being replaced).

# The Go rule (replaced; know it to read the fixtures)
`extractLastUserText`: decode `{messages:[{role, content}]}` (case-insensitive keys), walk from last to first, take the first `role == "user"` (case-sensitive), use its string content or the concatenation of `type == "text"` parts, cap at 100,000 Unicode scalar values. Empty -> declared fallback workload. No system prompt, no tools, no multi-turn context. Cases: `unit.json#extract_last_user_text-*`. These rows get a D5 tag and a Rust expected output.

# Required content (fixed by the spec)
- Include: system/developer instructions; bounded recent conversation text (not only the last user message); the response-format schema; tool names and descriptions.
- Exclude binary content (images, audio, file parts, and base64 payloads).
- Truncate per spec §8.3: oversize input uses head 80,000 + tail 20,000 Unicode scalar values; confidence is capped at 0.8 by the engine.
- A projection version string is sent as `workload.projection_version`; the engine folds it into the classification cache key.
- `X-Maverick-Workload: <capability>[:<tier>]` selects the declared form instead (Go forwarded that header upstream).

# The agent defines the exact format (no owner gate)
The spec fixes WHAT goes in, not the byte layout. The implementing agent defines the layout, names it version `p1`, and writes it down; it does not wait for approval, because the version is part of the cache key and a later change is a safe version bump. Required decisions, each written into a new "Projection format p1" paragraph in spec v1 §8.1 in the same commit:
- Section order and delimiters (suggested: `[system]`, `[response_format]`, `[tools]`, `[conversation]` headers, one blank line between sections; empty sections omitted).
- The "recent conversation" bound (suggested: the most recent messages, newest last, until 16,000 scalar values are used; always include the final user message in full up to the global cap).
- Role labels for each turn (suggested: `user:`, `assistant:`, `tool:`), how tool-call arguments and `tool_result` text appear (suggested: text included, JSON compacted), and how both surfaces (chat `messages` with `system`/`developer` roles, Messages top-level `system` string or blocks) map onto the same layout.
- Deterministic output: same input bytes -> same projection bytes, in every language.
The owner can review the written format at any time; review does not block this bead or its dependents.

# Tests (with detailed logging)
Golden `insta` fixtures for: single-turn, multi-turn, system + user, developer role, tool-use request with tool results, response_format schema, binary parts excluded, oversize truncation (both surfaces). On a mismatch the test prints the input, the expected and actual projection, and a diff. Export the same cases as conformance vectors (JSON) for the four SDKs. M6 gates on multi-turn and tool-use classification fixtures.

# Done when
Projection function + `p1` constant + spec paragraph + fixtures + vectors committed, D5 rows tagged. Commit.

title: Port prompt fingerprint, capture crypto with D18 key ring, and the capture decision
description:
# What
The prompt fingerprint, the debug-capture crypto with the new key ring (D18), and the pure capture decision. Reference Part 4 §4.1, §4.2, §4.4, §4.5; spec §10.1, §10.4. The DB-backed capture flow (insert, replay, reads, access log) is in the API package.

# Fingerprint (G5, G6)
`"hmac_sha256:" + lowercase_hex(HMAC-SHA256(key = tenants.prompt_hmac_key (32 random bytes minted at tenant creation), message = the prompt's exact UTF-8 bytes))`. No normalization, no trimming (NFC and NFD differ). The same value is the classification cache key, the response `prompt_hash`, and the trace column.

# Capture crypto
- Master key: `MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY`, exactly 64 hex chars = 32 bytes (config error text: `must be 64 hex characters encoding a 32-byte key`). Non-32-byte key at use: `tracing: capture master key must be 32 bytes, got %d`.
- Data key = HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869): IKM = master key, salt = UTF-8 bytes of the capture id (`cap_...`), info empty, length 32.
- AES-256-GCM, fresh 12-byte (96-bit) CSPRNG nonce per capture, no AAD, 16-byte tag appended. Stored: `ciphertext` = ct || tag, `nonce` = 12 bytes.
- Open failure: `tracing: decrypting capture %s: <gcm error>` (D36, owner-decided: keep the `tracing: decrypting capture <id>: ` prefix byte for byte; the tail after it is the Rust aead error text and is not compared).
- D18 key ring (new): current key (`MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY`, version `MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY_VERSION`, default 1) plus at most one previous key (`MAVERICK_CAPTURE_PREVIOUS_MASTER_KEY` as `version:hex`). Each capture stores `capture_key_version`. Encrypt only with the current key; decrypt by stored version. A retired key is dropped once `capture.max_window_minutes + capture.retention_hours` have passed since rotation.
- Use `subtle` for any secret comparison; zeroize keys in memory where practical.

# Capture decision (`Decide`)
`decide(windows, zero_retention, api_key_id, confidence, now)`: zero retention -> never. Else the first window in list order with `starts_at <= now < ends_at`, `api_key_id` null or equal, and `confidence_below` null or `confidence < confidence_below` (strict). No randomness. QUIRK: `confidence_below` is float32, so a window created with 0.95 compares against 0.949999988079071 (confidence 0.95 is NOT captured; 0.9499999 is). Reproduce.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/tracing_fingerprint.json` (7 rows; includes RFC 4231 test case 2, NFC vs NFD, empty prompt), `tracing_capture_crypto.json` (4 rows + fixed-nonce vectors), `tracing_capture_decide.json` (1 row + extra cases). New tests for the key ring: encrypt with v2, decrypt a v1 capture via previous key, reject unknown version, drop rule.

# Done when
All rows pass, key-ring tests added, mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port API key minting/hashing and internal token parsing with constant-time match
description:
# What
Pure auth primitives: API key minting and hashing, and internal token parsing and constant-time matching. The axum middleware that uses them (and the rate limiter) is in the API package. Reference Part 4 §5.1 and §5.3; spec §9.1, §13.

# API keys
- Raw key = `mk_live_` + base62(32 CSPRNG bytes), always 43 chars after the prefix (51 total).
- base62: treat the 32 bytes as a big-endian unsigned integer; repeatedly divide by 62, remainders are digits (least significant first) from the alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`; left-pad with `0` to 43 digits; most significant first. 32 zero bytes -> 43 zeros.
- At rest: `key_hash = SHA-256(raw key string bytes, including the prefix)` (32 bytes, bytea); `last4` = last 4 chars of the raw key. The raw key is shown once and never stored.

# Internal tokens
- `MAVERICK_INTERNAL_TOKENS` (required): split on `,`, trim each entry, split at the FIRST `:` into label and secret (both non-empty; a secret may contain `:`), else config error `must be a comma-separated list of "label:secret" pairs`.
- At startup store `SHA-256(label + ":" + secret)` per entry. A request bearer is hashed and compared against EVERY entry with a constant-time compare over the 32-byte digests (all entries always compared; the first match's label wins). The label is recorded as the acting party.

`parity/fixtures/decision/auth_keys.json` (4 rows). Manifest `decision.json` (auth package; the other auth rows that need a store are in the API auth-middleware bead).

# What
Per-run quality and pass, including the high-stakes overlay. Spec §6.1; reference Part 3 §1 "internal/scoring".

# Formulas
- `q_run = sum_d w_d * s_d` over PRESENT dimensions, renormalized over present dimensions (absent = grader error). Weights come from `tasks.dimension_weights`.
- `pass = (q_run >= task.pass_threshold)`. Feeds pass rates, ceilings, and prediction scoring.
- Truncated or refused outputs (`parse_failure`) are graded on whatever text exists; they count toward the column's parse-failure rate.
- High-stakes overlay (medical, legal, financial tags): weights are replaced by accuracy 0.40, calibration 0.20, hedging 0.15, citation honesty 0.25 (check the reference and `overlay.json` for the exact dimension names and mapping), and a failed `critical` rule or an `autofail` fact forces the run to fail (`q_run = 0`).

# Divergence D6 (important)
Go: provider errors and timeouts "score zero" (`q_run = 0`). Rust: a run with status `provider_error` or `timeout` has NO `q_run`. It is excluded from quality, counts as `pass = false` in pass rate (errors stay in the pass-rate denominator, so ceilings still penalize them), and counts against the new `availability` aggregate. Where a Go fixture asserts `q_run = 0` for an error run, assert the Rust rule and tag D6.

title: Implement maverick serve wiring: startup order, three process shapes, graceful shutdown
description:
# What
`maverick serve` wiring: startup order, listeners, process shapes, and graceful shutdown. Reference Part 1 §7.3 (exact order and log messages); master plan §4 (three shapes: `serve`, `serve --api-only` stateless replica, `serve --worker-only` exactly one).

# Order (Go, reproduce unless a DIVERGENCES row applies)
1. Flags `--api-only`, `--worker-only`; both set -> ERROR `serve: --api-only and --worker-only are mutually exclusive`, exit 2 (before config).
2. Load config (exit 1 on failure). INFO `starting maverick` with `public_addr`, `internal_addr`, `api_only`, `worker_only`.
3. Signal context (SIGINT, SIGTERM).
4. Create the DB pool lazily (an unreachable DB does not fail startup).
5. Provider clients for each provider with a non-empty key, in order anthropic, openai, xai, google. Google client failure logs and continues.
6. Alert fan-out (shared by workers and API). Failure exits 1.
7. Unless `--api-only`: grader registry (judge_rubric only if the judge pool resolves; else ERROR `judge pool unavailable; judge_rubric gradings will fail until it resolves` and continue), job client (cron parse errors exit 1), start workers, INFO `workers started`.
8. Unless `--worker-only`: classifier resolver; failure logs `classifier column unavailable; prompt-path requests will receive the fallback classification` and continues.
9. Listeners: internal ALWAYS (so `--worker-only` still serves health and operator surfaces), public unless `--worker-only`; internal first. INFO `listening` with `listener` and `addr`. Read header timeout 10 s.
10. Wait for the signal (INFO `shutdown signal received`, code 0) or the first listener failure (ERROR `listener failed`, code 1).
11. Shutdown with one 10-second deadline: graceful shutdown of each HTTP server, then stop workers, then wait for in-flight alert deliveries (drain the process-wide fan-out). INFO `stopped`.

# Shutdown of running jobs (QUIRK J9, covered by D10/D11)
In Go the River client got the signal context, so SIGTERM hard-cancelled running jobs, and a partial batch finished its tail and was never retried. The Rust design replaces this under D10 (batches lease, resume) and D11 (transactional failure tail): on SIGTERM, stop taking new jobs, let running handlers reach a safe point within the shared shutdown deadline, and do NOT mark an unfinished batch completed. Its `runs` stay, its lease expires or is recovered, and the next delivery resumes it under the same batch id. Tag the J9-related tests D10/D11. No further owner approval is needed.

# Also
Startup rejects a batch lease TTL that is not shorter than graphile_worker's earliest recovery threshold (spec §11.2). OTel exporter setup (fail-open; no public metrics endpoint).

# Depends on
CLI dispatch, config, the API server, the job client, alert fan-out, providers, classifier resolver.

# Done when
serve rows in `cli.json` pass and a process-level test starts both listeners, hits `/up`, and shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM. Commit.

JSON lines to stdout (INFO and above): `{"time":"<RFC3339Nano local>","level":"INFO|WARN|ERROR","msg":"...",<attrs in call order>}`; durations as integer nanoseconds; errors as strings. `mcp-stdio` logs to STDERR (stdout is the MCP channel; a test asserts stdout stays empty). title: Port the provider contract: types, error taxonomy, retry policy, settings helpers, scripted test server
description:
# What
The provider contract every client implements, the exact error taxonomy, the retry policy, settings helpers, and the scripted HTTP test server. Reference Part 2 §1 and §4 (exact strings and formulas).

# Contract
- `CompletionRequest { model, system, prompt, temperature: f32, max_tokens, settings: Map<String, Value> }`; `CompletionResponse { text, tokens_in, tokens_out }`; `trait ProviderClient { async fn complete(&self, req) -> Result<CompletionResponse, ProviderError> }`.
- Temperature is f32. Clients that send it as a JSON double widen it (`0.7f32 as f64` = 0.699999988079071); Google sends float32 and prints 0.7. QUIRK Q-P1. Wire cases `*_temperature_0_7`.

# Error taxonomy (exact)
Kind: unknown, invalid_request, rate_limited, provider_error, timeout. Display: `<provider>: <kind>` + ` (status <n>)` if status != 0 + ` after <n> attempt(s)` if attempts > 0 + `: <inner>` if inner. Example: `anthropic: rate_limited (status 429) after 3 attempt(s): slow down`.
`wrap_error(provider, status, err)`, first match wins: deadline or cancel in chain -> timeout (before status); 429 -> rate_limited; >= 500 -> provider_error; >= 400 -> invalid_request (includes 408); else (0 or 1xx-3xx) -> provider_error. Retryable: rate_limited and provider_error only. A non-provider error (kind unknown) is not retryable.

# Retry (exact)
Defaults MaxAttempts 3, BaseDelay 250 ms, MaxDelay 4 s, jitter uniform [0,1). `delay(attempt)`: d = MaxDelay; shift = attempt - 1; if 0 <= shift < 32 { exp = BaseDelay << shift (i64 ns, may overflow); if 0 < exp < MaxDelay { d = exp } }; half = d / 2 (integer ns); return half + (jitter * half as f64) as i64 (truncation). Wait is in [d/2, d). `retry(ctx, policy, fn)`: sets attempts on the error; returns non-retryable or exhausted errors; on deadline during backoff returns a timeout error with the provider name and attempts (text `test: timeout after 1 attempt(s): context deadline exceeded`). Inject the jitter source and a clock so tests are deterministic. SDK-internal retries do not exist (hand-written clients).

# Settings helpers
Key `response_schema` (only Anthropic acts on it via forced tool use; OpenAI/xAI/Google ignore it). `setting_bool`, `setting_string`, `setting_int` (accepts any JSON number and truncates toward zero; strings are absent). Consumed keys: Anthropic `thinking` + `thinking_budget`; OpenAI/xAI `reasoning` -> `reasoning_effort` verbatim; Google `thinking_budget` -> `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget`.

# Scripted test server (providertest)
An HTTP test server: records each request body; response i = script[min(i, len-1)]; optional per-response delay honoring cancellation (on cancel writes nothing); always `Content-Type: application/json`. Expose `calls()` and `last_request()`.

# D23
Clients take base URL and key only from engine config. No ambient env vars.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/providers_core.json` (12 rows: `internal/providers/errors_test.go` 4 + `retry_test.go` 8), including `#retry_delay_default_policy_probes` (jitter 0, 0.5, 0.999999; attempts 0..7, 31..64, -1).

# Done when
All rows pass. Mutants clean on the retry math. Commit.

description:
# What
The deterministic fake provider: the only "model" allowed in CI. Used by runner tests, job tests, the API end-to-end test, demo-run, and as the judge and classifier in tests. Reference Part 2 §3 (exact validation and error strings).

- Fixture files: `{"fixtures":[{"model","prompt"|"prompt_sha256","output","tokens_in","tokens_out","latency_ms","error"}]}`; all but `model` optional.
- Key = `model + "\x00" + sha256hex(prompt)` (lowercase hex of exact prompt bytes). `prompt_sha256` is used verbatim, so an uppercase hash never matches (QUIRK Q-F1; reproduce).

title: Port byte-identical prompt assembly (PromptText, Assemble)
description:
# What
Byte-identical prompt assembly for benchmark runs: the same bytes for every column, so differences in results come from the model, not the prompt. Reference Part 2 §5.1.

# PromptText(task)
- attachments = [] if task.attachments is empty bytes; else JSON-decode (error -> `parsing attachments: <err>`; JSON null -> empty; element fields `name`, `content`; unknown fields ignored; Go's case-insensitive field matching applies, so `Name` also matches; serde needs aliases or a custom decoder).

2. Settings: empty bytes -> none; else decode into a map (numbers become f64); error -> `column <column.id>: parsing settings: <err>`; JSON null or {} -> none; a JSON array is an error.
3. Returns `{model: column.model_id, system: "", prompt, temperature: task.temperature (f32), max_tokens, settings}`. The system slot is ALWAYS empty for benchmark runs.

title: Port the benchmark runner: worker pools, pacer, statuses, cost, run persistence, resume hook
description:
# What
The benchmark runner: executes a batch of (task x column x repeats), per-provider worker pools bounded by concurrency and requests per minute, sequential repeats, per-run timeout, status taxonomy, cost from the price snapshot, and one `runs` row per repeat. Reference Part 2 §5.2 to §5.7 (exact algorithm, texts, and the test catalog).

# Key rules
- Config: repeats (batch value if > 0, else `MAVERICK_RUNNER_REPEATS`, default 3); per-run timeout default 120 s (max 600 s); per provider `MAX_CONCURRENCY` default 8 and `RPM_LIMIT` default 0 (unthrottled).
- Skip columns whose status is not cold_start, active, or deprecated (log `skipping non-runnable column`); retired columns write no rows.
- Providers run concurrently; per provider, workers = min(max_concurrency, pairs); FIFO of pairs; one pacer per provider per run.
- All repeats of a pair run sequentially on one worker (repeats measure variance, not throughput).
- Setup error precedence and texts: attachments, settings, pricing (`parsing pricing snapshot: ...`, `pricing snapshot has a negative price`), client (`no provider client configured for "<provider>" (column <id>)`). A setup error writes a provider_error row per repeat with no latency and zero cost.
- execute: latency (ms, truncated) is set on EVERY executed row, success or failure. timeout if kind timeout or deadline in chain; else provider_error (rate limits, 5xx after retries, invalid request, unknown errors like a missing fake fixture). Success: status ok, output (even empty), tokens always set. The runner never writes parse_failure.
- Cost = round((in * p_in + out * p_out) / 1e6 * 1e6) / 1e6 with round half AWAY from zero (Go `math.Round`; Rust `f64::round` matches). Persist as decimal text with 6 places into `numeric(12,6)`. Summary cost = f64 sum of rounded per-run costs in completion order.
- Pacer: interval = 60 s / rpm in integer ns; first call claims now; each later start one interval after the previous claimed slot; a cancelled context fails even with no wait; a claimed slot is not given back.
- Persistence: one `InsertRun` per repeat immediately after it finishes (no batching, no transaction). Persistence failures are collected (`persisting run <id> (<task> x <column> repeat <n>): <err>`) and returned joined; provider failures never produce a returned error.
- Log `batch complete` with batch_id, runs_total, runs_ok, runs_error, spend_usd, duration_ms.

# Rust additions for the jobs package (D10)
The batch id comes from the caller (the deterministic batches id), not a fresh ULID, when the jobs package runs a batch. Support resume: skip (column, task, repeat) triples that already have a `runs` row for this batch id. Provide this as an input set of done triples, or a query hook, so the Go-parity tests still see Go behavior when the set is empty.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/runner.json` (9 rows) and `internal/runner/runner_test.go` (10 tests: taxonomy, skip retired, setup failure, concurrency bound and sequential repeats, pacer spacing, rpm limit, two Postgres batch tests, cost numeric round trip). Use tokio paused time for timing tests where possible so CI is not flaky.

# Done when
All rows pass. Commit.

title: Build the axum server skeleton: routers, middleware chain, wire encoding, strict decoding, error envelope
description:
# What
The axum server skeleton for both listeners: routers, the 404/405 behavior, the middleware chain, the exact JSON wire encoding, strict request decoding, and the error envelope with the full error catalog. Reference Part 5 §1 to §5 (exact); spec Appendix A and B.

# Routing (reference Part 5 §1)
Two independent routers. No redirects, no trailing-slash normalization, no HEAD-from-GET, no OPTIONS/CORS. Public `:8080`: `GET /up` (no auth), `any /mcp`, `/v1/config/{pools,weights,constraints}` GET/PUT, `GET /v1/policies`, `POST /v1/recommend`, `GET /v1/checks/*` (wildcard keeps slashes), `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/telemetry`, `/v1/history/*`, `/v1/debug/*`. Internal `:8081`: `GET /health/detail`, `/internal/v1/*` (Part 5 §1.2 table). Unmatched and wrong-method requests reach the 404 handler after RequestID, Logger, Recoverer (check the reference for whether wrong method is 404 or 405 in Go; chi returned 405 in some cases; the fixture `x_method_not_allowed` style rows and the replay decide).

# Middleware order (outermost first, both listeners)
1. RequestID: read `X-Request-ID`; if empty or > 128 bytes mint a ULID (26 chars, uppercase Crockford, monotonic); set the response header BEFORE the handler so every response (401/404/429/500) carries it.
2. Logger: one line per request (see the logging bead).
3. Recoverer: on panic log `panic recovered` with request_id, panic, stack; if nothing was written yet, write 500 `internal_error` / `internal error`.
4. Route match.
5. Public `/v1` and `/mcp`: Auth, then RateLimit, then BodyLimit (2 MiB = 2097152 bytes). Internal: InternalAuth for everything, then BodyLimit only under `/internal/v1`.
Consequences pinned by tests: an unauthenticated request never touches the limiter; a rate-limited request never has its body read; an oversize body with a valid key is counted by the limiter first, so the 413 carries `X-RateLimit-*`; 401/403 carry `X-Request-ID` but no rate-limit headers. Chunked (unknown length) oversize bodies must also 413 (`TestConfigOversizeBodyChunked413`).

# Wire encoding (Part 5 §3) and decoding (§4)
Every JSON body ends with exactly one `\n` (Go `json.Encoder`). Match Go's escaping (Go escapes `<`, `>`, `&` as `<` etc. by default; check the reference) and number formatting. Strict decoding: unknown fields rejected, trailing data rejected, as Go did. D25: `malformed request body:` prefix, status, and code match; the detail after the prefix is Rust's own text (tag D25).

# Error envelope and catalog (Part 5 §5)
`{"error":{"code","message","details":{}}}` exact, with every template the API writes (§5.2). Rust adds `409 no_compliant_columns` and `422 zero_retention_requires_declared`.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/api/apierrors.json` (4 rows), `middleware.json` (18 rows incl. rate limiter unit cases), `error_catalog_observed.json`, and `server_test.go` routing/body-cap rows (22 tests; auth and rate-limit rows are shared with the auth bead).

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement the MCP server with rmcp (streamable HTTP /mcp and mcp-stdio)
description:
# What
The MCP server with `rmcp`: streamable HTTP at `/mcp` on the public listener and stdio via `maverick mcp-stdio --api-key <key>`. Three tools that are thin wrappers over the same services as REST. Reference Part 5 §9 (exact identity, descriptions, schemas, result shapes, error texts); Part 1 §7.4 (mcp-stdio command); spec §12.

# Identity and tools
Implementation name `model-maverick`, version `v1`. Capabilities `{"logging":{},"tools":{"listChanged":true}}`. `tools/list` sorted by name: `get_policy`, `list_models`, `recommend_model`. Descriptions and input schemas are exact in `parity/fixtures/api/mcp.json` (`tools_list.result`); copy them byte for byte. The recommend tool must tell agents to prefer the declared workload form.

# Tool behavior
- `recommend_model`: same request type and pipeline as `POST /v1/recommend`; the raw arguments JSON is the trace `request`; writes the same `recommendations` row with the same tenant/key attribution.
- Success: `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"<REST body without the trailing newline>"}],"structuredContent":<same object>}`. Text must be byte-identical to the REST body minus `\n`.
- Caller mistakes (every 422 case): tool error `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"<code>: <message>"}],"isError":true}`. Other failures: `internal error` (log `mcp tool failure`). No session identity: `unauthorized: no authenticated tenant on this session`.
- Rust additions: the new 409/422 privacy codes surface as tool errors the same way.

# Schema validation error text (QUIRK Q7, D34 owner-decided)
Go used the Go MCP SDK wording, for example `validating "arguments": validating root: unexpected additional properties ["model"]`. Rust keeps the tool-error shape (`isError: true`, one text content item) and the `validating "arguments": ` prefix; the text after the prefix comes from the Rust libraries and must still name the offending property or path. No Go-wording formatter. Tests assert shape + prefix + named property; tag D34.

# Streamable HTTP
Behind Auth, RateLimit, BodyLimit (bad key -> REST 401 JSON envelope, not JSON-RPC; the limiter counts every MCP HTTP request). initialize -> 200 SSE with `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, `Connection: keep-alive`; notifications/initialized -> 202; tools calls -> 200 SSE with one `event: message` frame; DELETE -> 204. Per-message identity: every JSON-RPC message re-authenticates from its own HTTP request's Authorization header (`TestMCPToolCallsResolveTenantPerRequest`). Protocol version negotiated (recording shows `2025-11-25`).

# stdio
`mcp-stdio`: empty key -> ERROR `mcp-stdio: --api-key is required (spec §12)`, exit 2; config; pool; authenticate once (`mcp-stdio: authenticating --api-key`, exit 1); logs to STDERR only; stdout is the MCP channel and must carry nothing else. Known gap: stdio is described in prose only (no recording); test it in-process with an in-memory transport (`TestMCPStdioStyleTransportBindsRunContextIdentity`).

# Parity gate
`mcp_test.go` (9 tests), `parity/fixtures/api/mcp.json` (2 rows), MCP replay rows (SSE bodies).

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Build the black-box API replay harness (619 exchanges, 1,498 seed statements, masking)
description:
# What
The black-box replay test: the parity gate for the whole API. Apply `parity/blackbox/api-seed-sql.jsonl` and send `parity/blackbox/api-recorded.jsonl` in order against ONE database, comparing each response field by field with the masking rules in `parity/blackbox/README.md`. Master plan §7.0 step 2(d).

# Inputs
- `api-recorded.jsonl`: 619 exchanges (test, seq, gseq, listener public|internal, request {method, path, content_length, headers, authorization redacted by kind, body}, response {status, headers, body}).
- `api-seed-sql.jsonl`: 1,498 statements the TEST code ran (seeds, direct mutations, assertion reads) with bound args and Go types. Interleave by `gseq`. Reads may be used as post-condition checks.
- `api-timeline.md`: human view of the interleaving.
- README sections: record formats (§2), mapping records to tests (§3), fixed keys such as the capture master key (§4), truncated bodies and their exact generators (§5), masking rules.

# Harness design
- Rebuild each test environment the way Go did (`newTestEnv`, `newInternalEnv`, `newPromptEnv`, the e2e env, the closed-pool server): same config values (internal tokens `ops:alpha`, `rails:beta`; fixed capture master key), fake provider scripts for prompt tests.
- Auth: `minted_api_key` records hold `Bearer <api_key sha256=HEX>`. The raw key is not recorded; map by hash to the key the seed inserted (the seed stores `key_hash`), which means the harness must insert keys with known raw values or intercept auth by hash. Design this first; it is the hardest part.
- Replaying SQL from a Go-typed arg list: map `go_type` (`string`, `bool`, `int16`, `int32`, `float32`, `[]uint8`, `pgtype.*`) to sqlx binds exactly (float32 stays float32).
- Ignore server-set headers `Date`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`. Compare header names case-insensitively.
- Mask per README: request ids, generated ULIDs (map recorded id -> Rust id consistently across later requests), timestamps, rate-limit reset, etc.
- Map-order subtests: some Go tests iterate maps; their order in the recording is one run's order. The README and reference mark them; compare as sets.
- Rust schema is additive: seeds written for the Go schema must still apply.

# Expected diffs
Every diff must be fixed or matched to a DIVERGENCES row (D1, D2, D3, D4, D8, D9, D16, D18, D19, D20, D22, D25 can apply). Keep an explicit allowlist file mapping (test, seq) -> D-row, reviewed by humans. No unexplained diffs.

# Done when
The replay runs in CI (as an integration test against testcontainers Postgres) with zero unexplained diffs. Commit.

title: Implement the tenant telemetry opt-out (D39): constraint field, recommend 'telemetry' flag, engine-side drop
description:
# What
The engine side of the tenant telemetry opt-out (D39, owner decision 2026-09-28; spec v1 §9.10 "Tenant telemetry opt-out"; integration-surfaces plan §4 "honors a tenant-level telemetry opt-out (the proxy still routes but writes no outcome rows)").

# Why
The hosted trial proxy is operated by MM, so a tenant cannot use the proxy's global telemetry switch. G13 requires telemetry to be opt-out in every component. This gives each tenant its own switch, enforced in two places so a client bug cannot store the tenant's outcomes.

# Engine work
1. Schema: `tenant_constraints.telemetry_opt_out boolean not null default false` (additive migration; add it to the additive-migrations bead if still open, else a new migration).
2. Config: the constraints payload of `PUT /v1/config/constraints` and `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/constraints` accepts and returns `telemetry_opt_out`. It does not affect G4 simulation (not a column filter). Audit line `tenant.constraints.replace` covers it.
3. Recommend: every response carries `telemetry` (`false` when opted out, else `true`), next to `zero_retention`. Same field in the MCP `recommend_model` result (it mirrors REST).

title: Implement Auth, InternalAuth, and fixed-window RateLimit middleware
description:
# What
The Auth, InternalAuth, and RateLimit middleware. Reference Part 4 §5.2 to §5.4 and Part 5 §2.1 to §2.3.

# Public Auth (exact)
1. Header must start with exactly `Bearer ` (case-sensitive, one space), non-empty remainder, and the token must start with `mk_live_`; else 401 with NO store access.
2. Look up by SHA-256 of the token: no row -> 401; store error -> 500 (never an auth error).
3. Key status != active -> 401.
4. Tenant: no row -> 401; error -> 500; suspended -> 403.
Responses: 401 `unauthorized` / `missing or invalid API key`; 403 `tenant_suspended` / `tenant is suspended`; else 500 `internal_error` / `internal error`. Suspension turns keys off without touching data.

# InternalAuth
Bearer rule without the prefix requirement; hash and constant-time compare against every configured token (see the auth primitives bead); no match -> 401 `unauthorized` / `missing or invalid internal token`. Record the label as the acting party for audit.

# RateLimit (public only, after Auth)
`MAVERICK_RATELIMIT_RPM` (default 300) per API key id, fixed 1-minute windows aligned to wall clock, in memory, per process. Sweep old entries at most once per window. `allowed = count <= limit`, `remaining = max(limit - count, 0)`, reset = window start + 1 min. Every authenticated response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix seconds). Rejected: `Retry-After = max(ceil(seconds), 1)`, 429 `rate_limited` / `rate limit exceeded`, details `{"limit": <limit>}`. Rejected requests still count. Header name case: Go canonicalized to `X-Ratelimit-Limit` in recordings; HTTP header names are case-insensitive, compare that way.

# Parity gate
Auth rows of `parity/manifest/decision.json` (auth package, 13 tests incl. store-backed verification), `middleware.json` rate limiter cases, `server_test.go` auth and rate-limit rows. Use an injectable clock for the limiter.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement tenant config endpoints (pools, weights, constraints) with G4 validation

# What
Tenant configuration endpoints: `GET|PUT /v1/config/pools`, `GET|PUT /v1/config/weights`, `GET|PUT /v1/config/constraints`. Reference Part 5 §6.1 to §6.3 and §13.2; spec §9.7, §7.2; reference Part 1 §3 (transaction shape).

# Behavior
- PUT is a full replace. Transaction: validate (reads: pools, constraints, G4 simulation reads) -> on violations return without writing -> write -> commit. Pools write: delete all pools for the tenant, create each pool in request order, read back. Weights: delete then create each. Constraints: upsert.
- G4: pools and constraints are simulated together (the G4 simulation bead). Violation -> `422 pool_would_be_empty` naming pool and constraint. Unknown model in a pool -> `422 unknown_model`. Weights: `w_q + w_c + w_l = 1` (+/- 0.001) and `0 < quality_bar <= 1`, else `422 invalid_request`.
- Zero retention (D1) is part of the constraints payload and the simulation.
- Every endpoint shares the same validation code with the internal seam PUTs (`/internal/v1/tenants/{id}/{pools|weights|constraints}`), so no caller can create a configuration a tenant could not.

# Parity gate

# What

# Declared path (hot path)
auth -> validate -> policy (pool, allowlist, standing constraints incl. D1, preferences) -> rank from latest aggregates -> persist `recommendations` row -> respond. One aggregates read, one insert, no provider calls. Target p95 < 50 ms.
- Workload: exactly one of declared (`capability`, optional `difficulty` default 3 labeled as defaulted, optional `domain`/`domain_tags`) or prompt (the prompt path bead).
- Response: pick + chain; per entry `score` (display quality), `clears_difficulty`, `low_availability` (D8), `settings` and `retention_mode` (D9), `execution_aliases`, `reason`; top level `recommendation_id`, `matrix_version`, `constraints_met`, `violations`, `measured`, `check_spec` reference, `zero_retention` (always present, D9), `classification_quota_exceeded` only when hit (D4), `prompt_hash` on prompt form only.

- Errors: 422 invalid_request / unknown_model / model_not_in_pool / unknown_pool, 409 no_compliant_columns (D1), 413, 429.
- MCP must call the same service (an MCP recommendation writes an identical `recommendations` row).
