title: Implement the prompt path: classifier client, cache, D2 zero-retention column, D3 deadline, D4 budget
description:
# What
The prompt path of `POST /v1/recommend`: fingerprint, classification cache, classifier client, zero-retention classifier selection, the 1.5 s deadline, the classifier budget, the degraded alert, and the debug-capture hook. Reference Part 4 §3 and §4.5; Part 5 §6.5 and §13.5; spec §8.1 to §8.3; master plan §3.2.

# Flow
1. Fingerprint the prompt (per-tenant HMAC-SHA256; `prompt_hash` in the response).
2. Cache lookup on (tenant, prompt_hash, classifier version, projection version (D5)). Hit -> method `cached`.
3. Miss -> classifier call: small classifier column (default `claude-haiku-4-5/direct`, `MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_COLUMN`), temperature 0, structured output via forced tool call, fenced prompt (classifier pure-logic bead). Oversize prompts: head 80k + tail 20k runes, confidence capped at 0.8.
4. Result: capability, difficulty, domain tags, confidence; high-stakes derived from medical/legal/financial tags. Store in cache.
5. Continue as the declared path, persist the trace, then (after the trace insert) run the capture decision and, on a match, encrypt and insert the capture; every capture failure is logged (`debug capture failed; recommendation unaffected`) and swallowed.

# Divergences (all new in Rust)
- D2: for a zero-retention tenant use `classifier.zero_retention_column` (`MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_ZERO_RETENTION_COLUMN`, must have valid zero-retention evidence, validated under G4). If none is configured: `422 zero_retention_requires_declared` and the prompt NEVER leaves the engine (no classifier call, no cache write of the prompt, no capture).
- D3: one TOTAL deadline of 1.5 s (`MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_DEADLINE`) covering the call, one retry, and backoff, further bounded by the caller's remaining deadline when propagated. Go used 5 s per attempt x 2. On failure: `multi_step_reasoning` / 3 / confidence 0 / `fallback_default`.
- D4: per-tenant daily classification quota (engine default, operator override via `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/limits`) and a global daily classifier spend cap. Past either: `fallback_default` with `classification_quota_exceeded: true` instead of spending. Count usage in Postgres (no Redis), atomically, so multiple API replicas share it.
- D20: uncached prompt path p95 < 1.8 s (measured in the latency bead).
- Sustained classifier failure raises a critical `classifier_degraded` alert (degraded tracker).
- Classifier resolver failure at startup: serve continues; prompt requests get the fallback classification.

# Privacy tests (spec §15)
Neither classification nor recommendation sends a zero-retention tenant's prompt or pick to an unverified endpoint. Assert with the fake provider that no classifier call happens for a zero-retention tenant without a ZR column, and that the ZR column is the one called when configured.

# Parity gate
`recommend_prompt_test.go` (7 tests, including the high-stakes tag derivation subtests), classify rows in `parity/manifest/decision.json` that need a store or clock, replay rows. D2/D3/D4 tests are new.

# Depends on
2c provider contract and the fake provider (the classifier is a provider call).

# Done when
Rows pass; D2, D3, D4 tests added. Commit.

title: Implement tenant debug-capture endpoints (windows, replay, captures, prompt read, access log)
description:
# What
Tenant-facing debug capture: `POST /v1/debug/capture-windows`, `DELETE /v1/debug/capture-windows/{id}`, `POST /v1/debug/replay/{capture_id}`, `GET /v1/debug/captures`, `GET /v1/debug/captures/{id}/prompt`. Reference Part 4 §4.2 to §4.6; Part 5 §6.14 to §6.18, §13.9, §13.10; spec §9.8, §10.4; master plan §3.4.

# Why
The one support conversation this is built for: "your system keeps returning a small model where a large one was deserved." A tenant opens a time-boxed window (optionally one key, optionally only low-confidence classifications); matching prompts are encrypted per capture and hard-deleted at expiry (default 72 h). This is the ONLY place a prompt is ever stored (G5).

# Rules (exact in the reference)
- Window create: zero-retention tenants are refused (`409 zero_retention_conflict`); validation `422`. Window create and early end invalidate the per-tenant window cache (TTL 10 s).
- Replay re-runs classification in memory and returns `{original, replayed, match}` (match = same capability and difficulty), never the text. Missing: 410 `capture_expired` if a delete log row exists, else 404. Expired: log `read` then 410.
- Tenant prompt read: exact access-log rules (on miss log `read` with the CALLER's tenant id and the probed capture id). Every touch lands in `capture_access_log` (id prefix `cal`), which has no FK and outlives the capture. A log append failure fails the call.
- Capture decision uses the float32 `confidence_below` QUIRK.
- D18: new captures store `capture_key_version`; reads decrypt by stored version.
- Zero-retention tenants are also refused at the request-time capture decision.

# Parity gate
`capture_test.go` (21 tests), `capture_read_test.go` (9 tests), replay rows (the seed SQL reproduces ciphertext and nonces with a fixed master key; see `parity/blackbox/README.md` §4). D18 changes the stored shape: tag where needed.

title: Package 2d-Proxy: maverick-core crate and the trial proxy (maverick-proxy)
description:
# Goal
Build `crates/maverick-core` (the Rust copy of the shared SDK core) and `crates/maverick-proxy` (the trial proxy binary), and replay `parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json` (54 scenarios) against a mock engine and mock providers with zero unexplained diffs. Also pass `parity/fixtures/proxy/unit.json` and the `proxy` manifest (66 rows). HANDOFF §4 row 2d; master plan §3.5, §7.0 step 2(d). Reference Part 6; spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior".

# What the proxy is
A separate small binary with no database and its own deployment, so the engine stays control-plane pure. It speaks OpenAI chat completions (`POST /v1/chat/completions`) and Anthropic Messages (`POST /v1/messages`), so Anthropic-native tooling (Claude Code) works via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` unmodified. Per request: parse the alias (`maverick/auto`, `maverick/quality`, `maverick/cost`, `maverick/<pool>:<mode>`), project the request to a workload, ask the engine, walk the chain. URL interception is THE primary integration (decided 2026-07-15), so the proxy is the demo and the first real integration.

# Owner decisions (2026-09-28)
- Deployment: MM operates a shared HOSTED proxy and also ships the binary for self-hosting.
- Execution: direct (per-provider, caller credentials) by default; OpenRouter is opt-in.
- A "graduation link" response header is NOT built (nice-to-have, listed in `docs/features/proxy.md`).

# Divergences that land here
D5 (versioned workload projection), D12 (hosted mode reads no provider env keys), D13 (tenant key in `X-Maverick-API-Key` on hosted), D14 (apply column `settings` unless `?settings=caller`), D15 (OpenRouter ZDR per-alias retention; field `provider.zdr` verified), D16 (three-valued `check_pass`; absent when no check), D17 (zero-retention codes terminal, purge cache, fail closed), D19 (redaction), D26 (obey `Retry-After`), D27 (core telemetry batcher), D28 (per-tenant-key rate limit), D29 (catalog-driven parameter normalization, Go mappings as fallback), D30 (strip `X-Maverick-API-Key` upstream), D31 (OTel via tracing-opentelemetry), D32 (no Go identity headers), D38 (32 MiB body cap), D39 (tenant telemetry opt-out honored).

# Fences
No schema translation (the Messages surface executes Anthropic entries only). Direct execution by default. Tighter rate limits than the API. Body cap. No production SLA. The proxy is exempt from G14 fail-open by positioning, but privacy still fails closed.

# Depends on 2a (alias grammar, projection types). The replay uses a mock engine, so it does not need 2d-API to be finished; an end-to-end test against the real engine comes later (closeout bead and the full-stack e2e script).

title: Build the maverick-core recommend client (declared/prompt forms, terminal privacy errors)
description:
# What
The recommend client in `maverick-core`: the first piece of the shared SDK core (specified once, implemented four times in the SDKs, and in Rust for the proxy). Master plan §3.5 "The shared SDK core"; `plans/model-maverick-sdk-v0-plan.md` §2; reference Part 6 §7 (the Go proxy's engine call).

# Behavior
- `POST {engine}/v1/recommend` with `Authorization: Bearer <tenant key>`. Declared form (capability, difficulty, domain) or prompt form (the workload projection text plus `projection_version`). `X-Maverick-Workload: <capability>[:<tier>]` from the caller selects the declared form (D5).
- Timeout: 2 s for SDK cores (`MODELMAVERICK_*` config names: `_API_KEY`, `_BASE_URL`, `_TELEMETRY`, `_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `_PRIVACY`, `_EXECUTION`). The Go proxy used a 10 s engine timeout; pick per consumer (the proxy config sets its own), and note that the classifier's 1.5 s deadline is designed to fit inside 2 s.
- Response type: `recommendation_id`, chain entries with `provider`, `model`, `settings` (D14), `retention_mode` (D9), `execution_aliases` (each with retention, D15), `measured`, `classification.method`, top-level `zero_retention`, `classification_quota_exceeded`. Case-insensitive key match and zero values for missing keys, like Go (reference Part 6 §7 step 3).
- Error mapping: `422 zero_retention_requires_declared` and `409 no_compliant_columns` are TERMINAL privacy errors (typed), never fail-open triggers (D17). Other failures are "engine error".
- Request body for the Go-compatible proxy path: compact JSON, keys in lexicographic order, HTML-escaped strings (`a<b & c>d` -> `"a<b & c>d"`), pool omitted when empty. The declared fallback workload is `{"capability":"multi_step_reasoning","difficulty":3}`.
- Retries: none beyond one (sdk-v0 plan: fail-open is cheaper than resilience). The Go proxy did no retries.

# Rules
No provider schema translation. No disk state. Never send the caller's provider credential to the engine.

# Tests
Unit tests against a mock engine: both forms, header override, terminal errors typed, malformed engine JSON -> engine error. Replay rows from `scenarios.json` covering the engine call (for example `x_engine_malformed_json_502`, `x_engine_empty_chain_502`).

title: Implement OpenRouter execution mode with per-alias zero retention (D15)
description:
# What
The OpenRouter execution mode for `maverick-core` and the proxy, with the zero-retention rules (D15). `specs/model-maverick-openrouter-execution-spec.md`; master plan §3.6; `plans/model-maverick-openrouter-execution-plan.md`.

# Behavior
- Columns carry `execution_aliases` (at v0 one key: `openrouter` -> the OpenRouter slug), exposed on `GET /v1/models` and every recommend entry, so an SDK needs zero extra calls.
- In `execution: openrouter` mode the executor sends EVERY entry to one upstream (OpenRouter) with the entry's alias as the model slug and stamps `endpoint_used: openrouter`. Alias-less entries are skipped; an alias-less chain is `no_executable_candidates` (a catalog gap, not fail-open).
- One customer OpenRouter key replaces N provider keys. MM never holds OpenRouter keys and never proxies production traffic.
- D15 zero retention: each alias carries its own `retention_mode` with the same `retention_valid_until` expiry rule. For a zero-retention tenant, send OpenRouter's per-request Zero Data Retention option on EVERY attempt and skip any alias not verified `zero`. If nothing remains: `409 no_compliant_columns` (fail closed), NEVER a direct-key fallback.
- Hosted proxy: a caller OpenRouter key selects this mode for the request (D12).

# Settled details (2026-09-28)
- The ZDR field is verified against OpenRouter's provider-routing docs: send `"provider": {"zdr": true}` on every attempt for a zero-retention tenant. Keep it in one constant. (`provider.data_collection` is a different setting and is not sent.)
- OpenRouter is opt-in; direct execution is the default (owner decision).

# Tests
Conformance and proxy scenarios for a zero-retention tenant with an OpenRouter key: ZDR option present on every attempt, unverified aliases skipped, all-unverified -> 409, no direct fallback. Alias-less chain -> no_executable_candidates.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.

# What
The engine side of D29 (owner-approved 2026-09-28): per-model parameter constraints in the model catalog, carried on every recommend chain entry, so the proxy and SDK cores can normalize caller values to the nearest value the routed model accepts. Spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior"; `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` D29; master plan §3.5 ("catalog-driven per-model constraints are the durable form").

# Why
Go had two hard-coded mappings (chat `reasoning_effort` xhigh -> high; messages `output_config.effort` xhigh -> max). New models keep adding and removing effort tiers, so hard-coded mappings go stale. The catalog is data, edited through the internal seam, so constraints can change without a release.

# Design (propose, then build)
- Storage: an additive jsonb field on `model_columns`, for example `param_constraints`, default `{}`. Shape proposal: `{"<field>": {"allowed": ["low","medium","high"], "order": ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]}}` keyed by a surface-neutral field name (for example `reasoning_effort`), with an ordered scale so "nearest" is well defined (nearest by position in `order`, ties toward the lower value). Write the shape into spec v1 §3 and §4 with the migration.
- Additive migration only (D21). Add it to the additive-migrations bead if that bead is still open; else a new migration file.
- Internal seam: `POST /internal/v1/columns` and `PUT /internal/v1/columns/{id}` accept and validate the field (unknown field names and malformed shapes -> `422 invalid_request`); log `catalog_changes` with `change=param_constraints`.
- Recommend: every chain entry carries the column's constraints (next to `settings` and `retention_mode`). `GET /v1/models` exposes it too.
- `maverick-core`: a pure `normalize(field, value, constraints)` function shared by the proxy and the conformance vectors. With no constraint for the field, fall back to the Go mappings.
- Conformance: add vectors for normalization.

# Tests
Migration test; seam validation per error code; recommend and models response shape; normalization vectors (exact match, nearest down, nearest up, unknown value, no constraints -> Go fallback).

# Done when
Engine exposes the constraints, core normalizes with them, tests pass. Commit.

title: Build the maverick-core chain executor (advance rules, before-first-byte fallback, settings hook)
description:
# What
The chain executor in `maverick-core`, used by the proxy (and specified for the SDKs): walk the recommended chain, advancing on transient failures and stopping on the first relayable response. Master plan §3.5; spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior"; sdk-v0 plan §2.3 scenarios 2 to 5; reference Part 6 §8 (Go chain walk) and §16 (quirks).

# Rules
- Advance on 429, 5xx, timeout, connect error. NEVER advance on a semantic 4xx (400/422 etc.): relay it verbatim.
- D26 (owner-approved): on a 429, obey `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP date) before advancing. Bound the wait by the caller's remaining deadline; if the wait would exceed it, advance immediately and log why. Go ignored the header (QUIRK 11).
- Fallback happens only BEFORE the first byte reaches the caller. A 2xx is relayed or streamed the moment it is seen.
- Exhausted chain: SDK cores surface the last provider error; the proxy returns `502 no_executable_candidates` (surface-specific messages, exact in reference Part 6 §4) with `X-Maverick-Recommendation-Id` when non-empty.
- Skipped entries (no credential for that provider, alias-less in openrouter mode, retention not verified for a zero-retention tenant) produce no upstream request and no telemetry item.
- Per-attempt upstream response-header timeout 30 s; no limit on body duration after headers.
- `latency_ms` measures time to response headers (QUIRK 13).
- Client disconnect during the chain: Go classified every remaining entry as `connect_error` and wrote a 502 to the gone client (QUIRK 12). Keep the classification; stop dispatching further attempts once the disconnect is known (no DIVERGENCES row covers writing to a gone client, so match Go's telemetry).

# Settings (D14)
Before each attempt, apply the entry's `settings` unless the alias carried `?settings=caller`, and record `settings_applied`. Mapping settings to wire fields is the body-rewrite bead's job; this bead calls it.

# Tests (unit + scenario, detailed logging)
Conformance scenarios 2 to 5 (429 with Retry-After waits then advances, 500/timeout/connection refused advance, 400/422 no advance, exhausted chain) and proxy scenarios `x_chat_429_advances` (tag D26), `x_chat_connect_error_advances`, `x_chat_header_timeout_advances`, `x_chat_all_fail_exhausted_502`, `x_chat_404_relayed`, `x_chat_stream_after_503`. Use tokio paused time for waits. Each attempt emits a debug log line (entry index, provider, model, outcome, status, latency, wait applied) without bodies or credentials, and failing tests print the attempt log.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.

title: Build the maverick-core fail-open ladder with zero-retention rules (G14, D17)
description:
# What
The fail-open ladder and the zero-retention privacy rules in `maverick-core` (G14, D17). The SDK cores need this; the proxy is exempt from G14 by positioning but must still obey the privacy rules. Master plan §2 G14, §3.5; sdk-v0 plan §2.3 scenario 6.

# Ladder (G14)
An MM component failure never breaks the customer's LLM call: last-known-good chain -> static default (`MODELMAVERICK_DEFAULT_MODEL`) -> the original model string. `privacy: off` means MM is never contacted. In-memory only (no disk state).

# Zero retention (D17, privacy outranks G14)
- `422 zero_retention_requires_declared` and `409 no_compliant_columns` are terminal: surface the error, do NOT fail open, and PURGE the cached last-known-good chain for that tenant.
- Recommend responses carry `zero_retention: true` for such tenants: switch the core to declared mode and remember the tenant's zero-retention state in memory.
- During an engine outage for a zero-retention tenant: use only cached entries stamped `retention_mode: zero`; use the static default or original model only if locally configured as verified zero-retention; otherwise fail closed.

# Proxy position
The proxy is exempt from fail-open (an engine failure is `502 engine_error`, as Go did). It still must never route a zero-retention tenant's request to an unverified endpoint.

# Tests
Conformance scenario 6 in full: MM down -> cached chain; cold cache -> default model; privacy off -> MM never contacted; (a) terminal codes -> error surfaced, no fail-open, cache purged; (b) warm-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> only zero-stamped entries; (c) cold-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> fail closed unless the default is locally marked verified zero-retention.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.

title: Build the maverick-core telemetry producer (three-valued check_pass, settings_applied, off = zero bytes)
description:
# What
The telemetry producer in `maverick-core`, used by the proxy and specified for the SDKs. Master plan §3.5; spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior" (D27), §9.10; sdk-v0 plan scenarios 7 and 8; reference Part 6 §11 (the Go per-request telemetry being replaced).

# Item shape
`recommendation_id`, `model_used`, `status` (upstream status, 0 for transport error), `latency_ms`, optional `tokens_in`/`tokens_out` (only when parsed from a buffered 2xx with integer usage fields: chat `usage.prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`, messages `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`; null or non-integer -> absent; 0 kept), `error_class` (`timeout` | `connect_error`, transport errors only), `endpoint_used` (`direct` or `openrouter`), `check_pass` (D16: three-valued; ABSENT when no check ran, never defaulted to true; the proxy never runs checks, so it never sends it), `settings_applied` (D14).

# Delivery (D27, owner-approved; replaces Go's one-batch-per-request)
- A batcher: send every 10 s or when 20 items are queued, and flush on shutdown (bounded flush time, then drop). Fire-and-forget; failures are dropped silently (debug log only) and never affect the caller. No background threads beyond the batcher.
- One batch stream per tenant key (hosted proxy: the `X-Maverick-API-Key` of the request; self-hosted: the single configured key). Never mix tenants in one batch.
- Off means zero bytes: `MODELMAVERICK_TELEMETRY=off` (SDKs) and `MAVERICK_PROXY_TELEMETRY=off` (proxy; exact `off`, any case, QUIRK 19) create no batcher and open no connection.
- Skip items for requests where zero attempts were dispatched (Go rule).

# Tests (detailed logging)
`unit.json#parse_usage-*`; scenario 7 (shape, interval flush, size flush, exit flush, silent drop on failure, check_pass absent, settings_applied); scenario 8 (off = zero bytes asserted by the mock); proxy T-telemetry-off (zero `/v1/telemetry` calls in a 250 ms grace window); a two-tenant test proving batches never mix keys. Use paused time for intervals. Proxy scenarios whose telemetry timing differs from Go carry a D27 tag. Test failures print the captured batches.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.

title: Build the maverick-proxy shell: config, hosted/self-hosted mode, routing, pipeline, error envelope
description:
# What
The `maverick-proxy` binary shell: config loading, deployment mode, HTTP routing, the request pipeline with its error precedence, and the exact error envelope. Reference Part 6 §2 to §4 and §8 (cmd/maverick-proxy); fixture `unit.json#load_config-*`.

# Config (Go, exact)
Optional vars use the value only if present AND non-empty. `MAVERICK_API_KEY` (required; error `MAVERICK_API_KEY: required but not set` in self-hosted mode), `MAVERICK_ENGINE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8080`, strip ONE trailing `/`), `MAVERICK_PROXY_ADDR` (`:8090`), `MAVERICK_PROXY_TELEMETRY` (`on`; off iff exactly `off` any case), `MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_SERVICE_NAME` (`maverick-proxy`), `MAVERICK_UPSTREAM_{OPENAI,ANTHROPIC,GOOGLE,XAI}` with defaults (Google `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai`), env provider keys `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`.
Rust adds a deployment MODE fixed per deployment: `hosted` or `self-hosted` (D12, D13). Hosted: no `MAVERICK_API_KEY` needed (tenant keys arrive per request) and provider env keys are NEVER read (not even loaded). Self-hosted: Go behavior. Pick the env var name and default with care (self-hosted default keeps Go parity); document it.

# Routing (exact)
`GET /up` (also HEAD) -> 200 `{"status":"ok"}` with no trailing newline (Content-Length 15). `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/messages`. Wrong method on a known path -> 405 with `Allow`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, body `Method Not Allowed\n`. Unknown path -> 404 `404 page not found\n`. No trailing-slash variants.

# Pipeline (first failure decides)
1. Read body (error -> 400 invalid_request `failed to read request body`).
2. Decode `{model: string}` case-insensitively (error -> 400 `malformed JSON request body`; `null` body decodes to model "").
3. Parse alias (any error -> 400 `invalid_model_alias` with the exact message containing a raw U+2014 and escaped angle brackets, Content-Length 242). Engine not called.
4. Workload (projection, D5).
5. Recommend (failure -> 502 `engine_error`, log `maverick-proxy: engine recommend failed`; no telemetry, no OTel).
6. Chain walk.
Envelope: `{"error":{"code","message"}}` + `\n`, HTML-escaped strings.

# Server
Read header timeout 10 s. Body cap (D38, owner-decided): 32 MiB default via `MAVERICK_PROXY_MAX_BODY_BYTES`; a larger body (declared `Content-Length` or chunked, cut off while reading) gets `413` with the proxy envelope code `payload_too_large` before any engine or provider call. Graceful shutdown 10 s, then telemetry batcher flush and OTel flush; JSON logs to stdout; exit 1 on config, listener, or shutdown error.

# Owner decisions (2026-09-28)
Hosted plus binary: build both modes; MM runs a hosted instance. Execution is direct by default; OpenRouter is opt-in (in hosted mode a caller OpenRouter key selects it per request). A tenant with telemetry opt-out (D39) is still routed; only telemetry is suppressed.

# Parity gate
`unit.json#load_config-*`, scenarios `up`, `x_method_not_allowed`, `x_unknown_path_404`, `x_post_up_405`, `x_chat_invalid_json_400`, `x_chat_model_not_string_400`, `x_chat_missing_model_400_alias`, `x_messages_concrete_model_400`.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

Telemetry/OTel shutdown flush hooks arrive with 6.4 and the OTel bead.

Enforce on declared Content-Length and on chunked bodies while reading. Test both.

title: Implement proxy tenant auth (D13), credential resolution (D12), and upstream header rules
description:
# What
Tenant authentication (D13), provider credential resolution (D12), and upstream header rules for the proxy, including D30. Reference Part 6 §8.3 (`resolveKey`, `bearerToken`) and §9 (headers); master plan §3.5; spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior".

# Tenant auth (D13)
- Self-hosted: the single configured `MAVERICK_API_KEY` for every engine call (Go behavior).
- Hosted (one shared instance, owner-confirmed 2026-09-28): the tenant's Maverick key arrives per request in `X-Maverick-API-Key`. `Authorization` (chat) or `x-api-key` (messages) is reserved for the caller's PROVIDER credential. Rate limits (D28) and telemetry (D27) are per tenant key. Onboarding = base-URL swap plus one header (Claude Code: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` plus a custom header setting).
- Missing or malformed `X-Maverick-API-Key` on hosted: `401` with the proxy envelope `{"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"missing or invalid X-Maverick-API-Key"}}` + newline; the engine is not called. An engine 401/403 for that key maps to the same 401 (403 `tenant_suspended` is relayed as 403 with the engine's code). Record these strings in spec v1 §8.1 when implemented.
- Isolation tests: one tenant's key never recommends from another tenant's pools; telemetry goes out under the right key.

# Credential resolution
- Go `resolveKey(provider, native, clientCred)`: native provider with a client credential -> the client credential; else the env key for that provider (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`); "" -> skip. `bearerToken(h)`: "" if len <= 7 or the first 7 bytes are not `Bearer ` (case-insensitive); else the remainder unmodified. Messages surface: client credential = first `x-api-key` value as-is; a client `Authorization` is ignored for resolution and stripped. Cases `unit.json#bearer_token-*`.
- D12 hosted mode: reads NO provider env keys (they are not even loaded). Accepts a caller OpenRouter key (every entry executes through OpenRouter; OpenRouter bead) or a surface-native credential, in which case the chain is RESTRICTED to that provider's entries. Required test: a hosted instance given only an OpenAI key NEVER calls Anthropic.
- Self-hosted keeps env-key fallback (standard names, never `MAVERICK_`-prefixed).
- Keys live in memory for the request only; never stored, logged, or put in spans (G5).

# Upstream headers
Start from all client headers; drop headers named in any `Connection` value; drop the hop-by-hop set (`Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Authenticate, Proxy-Authorization, Te, Trailer, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade`); drop `Host, Content-Length, Authorization, X-Api-Key`; and (D30, owner-approved) drop `X-Maverick-API-Key`. Keep all other values in order (repeated `anthropic-beta`). Default `Content-Type: application/json` if missing. Chat sets `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; messages sets `X-Api-Key` and defaults `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`.
The engine key and the tenant key must never appear in any upstream header (Go tests assert `mk_live_test` appears nowhere upstream; extend the assertion to the hosted tenant key).
Runtime identity headers (D32, owner-decided): send no Go transport or identity headers (no `User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1`, no forced `Accept-Encoding: gzip`); use the reqwest defaults. Scenario comparisons ignore identity and transport headers.

# Tests (detailed logging)
`unit.json#bearer_token-*`, `#build_upstream_headers-*` (tag `build_upstream_headers-2` D30); scenarios `chat_hop_by_hop_stripped`, `messages_client_authorization_stripped`, `chat_client_x_api_key_stripped`, `x_chat_no_credential_502`; new hosted-mode, isolation, missing-tenant-key, and key-never-upstream tests. On failure print the full upstream header list with credential values redacted.

# Done when
Rows pass and new tests pass. Commit.

Spec 8.1 records the strings.

title: Implement the chat and messages surfaces: dispatch, streaming/buffered relay, correlation headers
description:
# What
The two proxy surfaces on top of the chain executor: URL building, per-entry dispatch, streaming and buffered relay, and correlation headers. Reference Part 6 §8.1, §8.2, §8.4, §8.5, §9.2, §9.3, §15, §16.

# Chat (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, native provider openai)
Upstream URLs: openai `{UP_OPENAI}/v1/chat/completions`, anthropic `{UP_ANTHROPIC}/v1/chat/completions`, google `{UP_GOOGLE}/chat/completions`, xai `{UP_XAI}/v1/chat/completions`; append `?` + raw query when non-empty. These are the providers' own OpenAI-compatible endpoints; the proxy never translates schemas.

# Messages (`POST /v1/messages`, native provider anthropic)
Every attempt goes to `{UP_ANTHROPIC}/v1/messages`. Entries whose provider is not exactly `anthropic` are SKIPPED (no translation).

# Dispatch outcomes
Transport timeout (incl. the 30 s response-header timeout) -> status 0, `timeout`, advance. Other transport error -> 0, `connect_error`, advance. 429 or >= 500 -> drain, advance. Anything else (1xx/2xx/3xx/4xx except 429) -> relay and stop.

# Relay
- Set `X-Maverick-Recommendation-Id` (even when empty, QUIRK 1) and `X-Maverick-Model-Used` (the executed model) BEFORE upstream headers; upstream headers are ADDED after, so an upstream `X-Maverick-Model-Used` yields two values (QUIRK 2).
- Streaming iff 2xx AND the first `Content-Type` value (ASCII-trimmed) starts with `text/event-stream` (case-sensitive; `Text/Event-Stream` is buffered, QUIRK 8). Copy headers except hop-by-hop, stream bytes unchanged with a flush after every write (no SSE parsing). No Content-Length. Mid-stream upstream abort -> the client sees a normally terminated response (QUIRK 9; no DIVERGENCES row covers it, so match Go: relay what was received and end the response normally; telemetry records the upstream status). Tokens are not parsed on the streaming path.
- Buffered otherwise: read the whole body (read error -> empty body with the upstream status and headers incl. its Content-Length, QUIRK 10); parse usage on 2xx.
- The request's `stream` field plays no role.
- Correlation headers are not set on 400, 502 engine_error, or /up.
- Upstream redirects are followed (POST -> GET on 301/302/303, QUIRK 17). reqwest follows redirects by default with a limit of 10; match Go's method rewriting.
- Upstream client ignores HTTP_PROXY env; HTTP/2 via ALPN; at most 2 idle connections per host.

# Parity gate
Chat and messages scenarios in `parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json`, including `x_chat_google_xai_paths`, `x_chat_stream_after_503`, `x_messages_streaming_sse`, `x_messages_mid_stream_abort`, `x_chat_sse_content_type_case`, `x_chat_upstream_sets_maverick_header`, `x_chat_404_relayed`.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

Failures print the upstream request, the upstream scripted response, and the client-visible response bytes with a diff (bead 1.7).

title: Implement byte-exact body rewrite, parameter normalization, and D14 settings application
description:
# What
Body rewrite for each attempt: replace `model`, normalize model-dependent parameters (D29), apply the entry's `settings` (D14), and re-encode exactly as Go did. Reference Part 6 §10; spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior"; master plan §3.2, §3.5.

# Go rewrite (byte-exact, `unit.json#rewrite_model-*`)
1. Decode the body into top-level key -> RAW JSON value (error if not an object; duplicate keys: last wins).
2. Set `model` to the JSON encoding of the entry model (HTML-escaped). Only the exact lowercase `model` key is replaced; `MODEL` stays too (QUIRK 4).
3. Normalization (below).
4. Re-encode: top-level keys sorted by byte value; ALL whitespace removed, including inside nested raw values; inside strings `<` `>` `&` become `<` `>` `&` and U+2028/U+2029 become escapes; everything else in raw values is kept byte for byte (number spellings like `0.50`, `1e2`, existing `\uXXXX`, non-ASCII UTF-8, nested key order).
serde_json will not do this by default. Use `serde_json::value::RawValue` per top-level key plus a small byte-level compactor/escaper that tracks string state. Property-test it (compaction never changes the parsed value).

# Normalization (D29, owner-approved, catalog-driven)
- Each chain entry carries per-model parameter constraints from the catalog (engine side: bead 6.14). Call the shared `maverick-core` `normalize(field, value, constraints)` function: map the caller's value to the nearest value the routed model accepts.
- When the entry has no constraint for a field, apply the Go mappings: chat top-level `reasoning_effort` `xhigh` -> `high`; messages `output_config.effort` `xhigh` -> `max` (when it fires, `output_config` is re-encoded with sorted keys and siblings keep their raw bytes: `{"effort":"xhigh","custom_ratio":0.50, "b" : 1}` -> `{"b":1,"custom_ratio":0.50,"effort":"max"}`).
- Never add a missing field during normalization.
- Build and test against mock-engine chain entries; this bead does not wait for bead 6.14, which supplies the real engine data.

# Settings (D14)
Unless the alias had `?settings=caller`, apply the entry's `settings` (reasoning effort, thinking mode) in the surface's wire fields (chat: `reasoning_effort`; messages: the Anthropic `thinking` object and/or `output_config.effort` as the Anthropic API defines them). Settings are applied BEFORE normalization, so the result is always a value the model accepts. Record `settings_applied`. Keep the settings -> wire-field mapping in one table with a test per provider; where the provider docs do not define a field, leave it untouched and log at debug.

# Tests (detailed logging)
`unit.json#rewrite_model-*`, scenario `x_chat_body_reencoding`, normalization cases (constraint present: exact, nearest down, nearest up, unknown value; constraint absent: Go fallback), settings cases (applied, `?settings=caller` leaves the caller's values). Failing tests print input body, expected and actual bytes, and a byte-level diff.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-28: D29 approved, catalog-driven. Normalize caller model-dependent values (effort tiers etc.) to the nearest value the routed model accepts, using per-model constraints carried on each chain entry. When the entry has no constraint for a field, apply the two Go mappings (chat reasoning_effort xhigh->high; messages output_config.effort xhigh->max). Engine side (catalog field, API exposure) is a separate bead; build against the entry field and test with mock-engine data.

title: Wire proxy telemetry, optional OTel emission, and per-tenant rate limiting
description:
# What
Proxy telemetry wiring to the engine, OTel emission (D31), and per-tenant rate limiting (D28). Reference Part 6 §11 to §13 and §18 (T-otel-* tests); spec v1 §8.1 "Trial proxy behavior"; master plan §3.5, §6.

# Telemetry wiring
Use the maverick-core producer (D27). One item per dispatched attempt in chain order; skipped entries produce none; `endpoint_used` is `direct` (or `openrouter` in that mode). Items are enqueued after the relay completes (after the whole stream for SSE). Never on 400 or `engine_error`.

# OTel (D31, owner-approved)
- Enabled iff `MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is non-empty; disabled means no exporter task and no connection (T-otel-disabled: the collector receives 0 requests in 250 ms).
- Export through `tracing-opentelemetry` + `opentelemetry-otlp` (HTTP), service name `MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_SERVICE_NAME` (default `maverick-proxy`), W3C trace context propagated to the engine and to the provider call.
- Keep the Go CONTENT: one log record per settled request with body `maverick.recommendation` and attributes recommendation id, surface (`chat_completions` | `messages`), mode, model, attempts, final_status, measured, classification_method; and a cumulative monotonic counter `maverick_proxy_recommendations_total` with attributes `measured` and `classification_method` (Go used string `"true"`/`"false"` on the counter, QUIRK 18; keep strings). Payload bytes are not reproduced (D31): tests parse the OTLP payload and assert content, not bytes.
- Fail-open: an exporter error never affects a request. Flush on shutdown with a bounded timeout.

# What
The job client on `graphile_worker` 0.13.x: job kinds, args, cron schedules and the engine's cron parser, enqueue keys, per-kind `max_attempts` and timeouts, and startup validation. Reference Part 3 §2.2, §2.3 (River config and semantics the Go code relied on), cron evaluation; spec §11, §11.2; D10, D22.

# Job kinds (exact spellings) and args JSON (exact keys)
`prediction_lock {night}`, `nightly_smoke {night}`, `weekly_sweep {week: "YYYY-Www", night}`, `aggregate_rebuild {night, batch_id}`, `regression_scan {night, batch_id}`, `calibration_score {night, batch_id}`, `latency_probes {hour: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH"}`, `price_sync {day}`, `catalog_sync {day}`, `capture_expiry {hour}`, `history_prune {day}`. prediction_lock `50 2 * * *` (`MAVERICK_CRON_PREDICTION_LOCK`), nightly_smoke `0 3 * * *` (`MAVERICK_CRON_NIGHTLY`), weekly_sweep `0 4 * * 0` (`MAVERICK_CRON_WEEKLY`), latency_probes `0 * * * *`, price_sync `0 6 * * *`, catalog_sync `10 6 * * *`, capture_expiry `0 * * * *`, history_prune `0 5 * * *`. 5 fields; parts `*`, `N`, `A-B`, `*/S`, `N/S`, `A-B/S`; dow 7 folds to 0; exact errors (`invalid step %q`, `invalid value %q`, `invalid range %q`, `value out of range %d-%d: %q`, `empty field %q`, `cron %q field %d: <msg>`, `cron %q: want 5 fields, got %d`); dom/dow star rules; `Next` returns the 5-year horizon for impossible schedules (QUIRK J1); `cronFiresOn(expr, night)`. `job_key = "<kind>:<window>"` as a first filter only. `max_attempts`: batch kinds 3; chained and hourly kinds 5; never graphile's default 25. Go's weekly_sweep was unique on `week` only (QUIRK J2): the Rust window for weekly_sweep is the ISO week; confirm with the reference and keep the same collapse behavior.

Batch kinds: `MAVERICK_BATCH_JOB_TIMEOUT` (default 6h, max 24h). Chained and hourly (rebuild, scan, calibration, probes): 15 min. Reject a batch lease TTL that is not shorter than graphile_worker's earliest stale-job recovery threshold. Worker concurrency: Go ran one queue with 10 workers.

`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/cron.json` (5 rows: accept, reject with exact errors, Next, fires_on, iso_week); timeout-pin tests and bad-cron tests from reference Part 3 §6 (TestNewClientRejectsBad*Cron, Timeout pins; restate them against the Rust config).

title: Implement capture_expiry and history_prune
description:
# What
`capture_expiry` (hourly) and `history_prune` (05:00). Reference Part 3 §2.14, Part 4 §4.7, Part 1 §3; spec §10.3, §10.4.

# capture_expiry (one transaction)
Delete debug captures with `expires_at <= now` (returning id, tenant_id); for each insert a `capture_access_log` row (actor `capture_expiry`, action `delete`); delete capture windows with `ends_at <= now - capture.retention_hours` (default 72 h); commit. Output `{deleted_captures, deleted_windows}`.

# history_prune (one transaction)
`cutoff = now - history.retention_days` calendar days (default 365, `MAVERICK_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS`). Delete captures of recommendations with `created_at < cutoff` (each logged, actor `history_prune`), then outcomes of those recommendations, then the recommendations; commit. Aggregates, calibration, and the access log are NEVER pruned (they are the product and the audit trail). Output `{cutoff (RFC 3339), deleted_recommendations, deleted_outcomes, deleted_captures}`.

# Failure
Both write `job_failure` warning with subject `{error, job, hour|day}` and message `%s failed: %v`, then return the error (retry). In Rust write the alert in its own transaction after the failed one rolls back.

# D18 note
Key ring rotation rule: a retired master key is dropped once `capture.max_window_minutes + capture.retention_hours` have passed since rotation. capture_expiry guarantees no capture outlives that window, which is what makes the drop safe. Add a test that ties the two.

Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement alert insert and the process-wide SMTP + HMAC webhook fan-out with shutdown drain
description:
# What
Alerts: the row-first insert helper and the process-wide asynchronous fan-out to SMTP email and an HMAC-signed operator webhook, shared by job writers and request-time writers, drained at shutdown. Reference Part 3 §4 (exact wire formats) and §2.15; spec §11.1; master plan §3.4.

# Kinds (closed enum)
`regression`, `parse_failure_rate`, `job_failure`, `spend_warning`, `spend_refusal`, `pool_would_be_empty`, `classifier_degraded`, plus Rust `retention_expiring`. Severity CHECK: info|warning|critical. IDs `alr_` + ULID. Model the kind as a serde enum.

# Insert
`insert_alert(kind, severity, subject, message)`: serialize the subject (error `jobs: encoding %s alert subject: %w`), insert returning the row (error `jobs: writing %s alert: %w`, no notify), then notify with the RETURNED row (so the subject is Postgres jsonb text). Notify never blocks or fails the caller. For writes inside a transaction (D11 batch tail), notify after commit.

# Fan-out
Destinations in order: email (if `MAVERICK_SMTP_URL`), webhook (if `MAVERICK_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL`). Per destination an independent task: up to 4 attempts, sleeping 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (no jitter); each attempt has a fresh 30 s timeout not tied to any caller; logs `alert delivered`, `alert delivery attempt failed`, `alert delivery failed`. `wait()` blocks until in-flight deliveries finish (no deadline; QUIRK A3); serve and mcp-stdio call it at shutdown.

# Webhook (exact)
URL scheme http/https; secret required. POST, `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Maverick-Signature: sha256=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, exact body bytes)>`. Body fields in order `{"id","kind","severity","subject","message","created_at"}`; subject is the stored jsonb text inserted raw but compacted and HTML-escaped; created_at RFC 3339 UTC with trailing fractional zeros trimmed; strings HTML-escaped (QUIRK A2: `>` escaped, and the signature covers escaped bytes). Success = any 2xx; else `webhook responded %d`; read and discard up to 4096 bytes.

# Email (exact)
`smtp://[user:pass@]host[:port]/?from=<addr>&to=<a>[,<b>]`; port default 587; STARTTLS if advertised; AUTH PLAIN only after TLS (or localhost); exact error prefixes and message format (CRLF; `Subject: [maverick] <severity>: <kind>`; RFC 1123 Date with numeric zone; body = message, blank, `alert: <id>`, `subject: <jsonb text with spaces>` (QUIRK A1)). Consider `lettre` with rustls; keep the conversation and bytes matching the fixture.

title: Write the job crash/restart acceptance tests (kill -9, recovery with live lease, re-enqueue, timeout)
description:
# What
The job crash and restart acceptance tests. Spec §11.2 "Acceptance"; master plan §3.1 and §11 ("the queue gets its own crash and restart tests").

# Scenarios (real Postgres, real graphile_worker, fake provider with latency so batches take time)
1. `kill -9` of the worker process mid-batch, then restart.
2. `kill -9` where graphile_worker's recovery fires while the application lease is still live.
3. A plain restart (graceful stop) mid-batch.
4. An enqueue of the same (kind, window) while the batch is running.
5. An enqueue of the same (kind, window) after it completed (graphile has already deleted the completed job).
6. A handler timeout (per-kind `tokio::time::timeout` shorter than the batch).

# Every scenario must end with
No permanently failed jobs left behind; exactly one completed batch per window; exactly one rebuild; no duplicate persisted runs or aggregate contributions (check the unique index and the aggregates row counts); the correct alerts (for example a job_failure for a sub-90% completion only when that is true).
Duplicate provider calls are allowed only when a crash lands between a successful call and its runs commit; assert they are bounded (count fake-provider calls) and accounted by the spend guard.

# How to kill
Run the worker as a child process (the `maverick serve --worker-only` binary or a test binary) and send SIGKILL. Use short lease TTLs and graphile recovery settings in tests, respecting the startup rule (lease TTL shorter than recovery threshold).

# Done when
All six scenarios pass reliably (run each at least 20 times locally before closing to catch flakiness). Commit.

title: Implement the batches lease: claim, no-op outcomes, takeover, heartbeat, deterministic id (D10)
description:
# What
The engine-owned `batches` lease that gives every job per-(kind, window) uniqueness (D10). This replaces River's unique jobs, because graphile_worker deletes completed jobs, so its `job_key` cannot stop a re-enqueue after completion from running a second time. Spec §11.2; master plan §3.1.

# Claim (first transaction of every handler)
Insert the `batches` row for (kind, batch_window) if absent: deterministic `id`, `status = running`, `lease_owner` = the graphile_worker worker id, `lease_expires_at`, `heartbeat_at`, `attempt = 1`. Or take it over if its lease expired. Outcomes:
- `completed` or `skipped` row -> the handler is a no-op and returns success.
- Live lease held by a different worker that is still alive -> return success as a no-op. NEVER fail (a failure would burn `max_attempts` into a permanent failure). Nothing is stranded: the holder's own job stays locked, and graphile recovers it if the holder dies.
- Owner gone (graphile recovered the job from that worker) -> take over IMMEDIATELY, even before `lease_expires_at`. Determining "owner is gone" needs graphile_worker's worker/lock state; read how 0.13.x records locked_by and recovery, and base the rule on that.
- Stale running row -> take over; `attempt` increments; the batch resumes under the SAME id from its existing `runs`.

# Heartbeat
The holder renews `lease_expires_at` and `heartbeat_at` well inside the expiry (for example every TTL/3). If a renew finds the lease lost, stop work promptly.

# Resume and idempotency
Delivery is at-least-once, so every handler is idempotent: a batch resumes by skipping (column, task, repeat) triples that already have a `runs` row for this id (the runner's resume hook); the rebuild is keyed by batch. A spend refusal records the window as `skipped`.

# Deterministic id
`bat_` + a deterministic ULID-shaped value from (kind, window) (for example a hash-derived 128-bit value), equal to `runs.batch_id` for batch kinds. Document the derivation; it must be stable across processes and releases.

# Tests (real Postgres)
Concurrent claimers: exactly one runs. Completed -> no-op. Live foreign lease -> no-op success. Expired lease -> takeover with attempt 2 and same id. Heartbeat renewal. Lease-lost detection.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.

title: Wire the G8 spend guard into batches (window actuals, refusal -> skipped, 80% warning)
description:
# What
The G8 spend guard as it runs inside batch jobs: projection plus window actuals against the nightly and weekly caps, refusal and warning alerts, and the skipped batch. Reference Part 3 §2.6 (exact formulas, subject keys, message formats) and §6 spend guard tests; spec §11.

# Rules
- Projection from the domain bead (`ProjectSpend`): runes not bytes; `est_in = (runes + 3) / 4 + 600`; per_run = (est_in * in_price + max_tokens * out_price) / 1e6; x repeats; pricing error text `jobs: projecting spend: column %s: %w`.
- Windows over `runs.ran_at` (half-open): nightStart = night 00:00 UTC, nightEnd = +1 day, weekStart = nightStart - 6 days. `nightTotal = nightSpent + projected`, `weekTotal = weekSpent + projected`.
- Refuse iff `(applyNightly && nightTotal > nightlyCap) || weekTotal > weeklyCap` (strict). applyNightly is false for weekly_sweep. Insert `spend_refusal` critical; the batch does not run; record the window as `skipped` (D10).
- Else warn iff `(applyNightly && nightTotal >= 0.8 * nightlyCap) || weekTotal >= 0.8 * weeklyCap`: `spend_warning` warning; run. QUIRK J7: cap 0 with a zero projection fires a warning.
- Subject keys: `job, night, nightly_cap_usd, night_spent_usd, planned_runs, projected_usd, weekly_cap_usd, week_spent_usd`. Messages exact (reference; `spend.json#messages`), including `(≥80%)`.
- A failed alert insert returns `jobs: writing %s alert: %w` and the job retries.
- Actual spend accumulates per batch so projections are auditable (batch output `projected_usd`, `actual_usd`).
- Duplicate provider calls after a crash (between a successful call and its runs commit) are bounded by this accounting.

`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/spend.json` (2 rows) and the five DB tests: refuses over nightly cap, refuses over weekly cap, warns at 80%, allows under cap, sums window actuals.

title: Implement nightly_smoke and weekly_sweep: composition, resume, grading pass, transactional failure tail (D11)
description:
# What
The `nightly_smoke` and `weekly_sweep` handlers: batch composition, the prediction-lock precondition, the spend guard, execution through the runner with resume, the grading pass, completion accounting, and the failure tail written in the same transaction as the batch outcome (D11). Reference Part 3 §2.4, §2.5, §2.7; spec §11; master plan §3.1.

# Composition
- nightly_smoke: tasks = active tasks of the active corpus (by id); columns = runnable (cold_start, active, deprecated; by id). Groups: (smoke-member tasks x non-cold columns) then (ALL tasks x cold_start columns). Both caps apply.
- weekly_sweep: (all tasks x all runnable columns), weekly cap only, full-length long-context tasks.
- repeats = `MAVERICK_RUNNER_REPEATS` (3 if <= 0).

# Steps
1. Claim the `batches` lease (lease bead). No-op outcomes return success.
2. Project spend over groups (error -> job error/retry). Zero planned runs -> log `batch has nothing to run`, output `{completion_pct: 1}`, mark the window completed, no rebuild.
3. Lock precondition: count predictions for the night; zero -> warn `no predictions locked for tonight; batch proceeds unscored (spec 11 prediction_lock)`, `lock_missing: true`, continue.
4. Spend guard: refused -> `refused: true`, window `skipped`, no runs, no rebuild.
5. batch_id = the deterministic `batches.id` (D10; Go minted a fresh `bat_` ULID per execution). Run each group through the runner with resume (skip triples already in `runs`). Runner persistence errors are logged, not returned. Heartbeat the lease throughout.
6. List runs by batch; grade every run with output (grading pass below).
7. completed_runs = runs with status ok or parse_failure; completion_pct = completed / planned.
8. Failure tail + outcome in ONE transaction (D11): mark the batch `completed`, write `job_failure` warning if completion_pct < 0.9 (strict; message `%s %s completed %d/%d runs (%.1f%%)`), write `job_failure` warning if judge failures / attempts >= 0.1 (message in the reference, threshold printed as 10), and enqueue `aggregate_rebuild {night, batch_id}` using graphile_worker's SQL `add_job` inside the same transaction. No detached tasks carry durable work. Alert fan-out (email/webhook) happens after commit and never blocks.
9. Return success once runs exist (never retried after that), with the batch output `{batch_id?, refused?, lock_missing?, spend_warned?, projected_usd, actual_usd, planned_runs, completed_runs, completion_pct, graded_runs, judge_attempts?, judge_failures?}`.

# Grading pass (reference §2.7)
For each run with output (order task_id, column, repeat): find the task (unknown -> log, skip); decode grader specs (fail -> log, skip); per envelope: parse; judge -> count attempt; grade (error -> judge failure if judge, warn, skip; dimensions absent); map dimensions; empty -> skip; `SaveScores(run, idx, mapped, detail)`. A run with any saved grader counts as graded. On resume, do not re-grade runs that already have scores (idempotency); check the reference for Go's behavior and document the Rust rule.

# Go quirks to review
J3 (expired context makes completion 0%) and J9 (SIGTERM cancels running jobs and the partial batch completes and is never retried). With the lease and resume, the Rust behavior improves on both; these changes fall under D10/D11. Record them in the tests with D10/D11 tags.

# Parity gate
Reference Part 3 §6 batch tests (TestFinishBatch* restated for the transactional tail), `parity/manifest/measurement-core.json` jobs rows. Sunday: both batches for the same night, two rebuilds with distinct batch ids.

# Done when

title: Implement aggregate_rebuild (bit-exact f32 fold, D6 availability, D7 censored latency, chained enqueue)
description:
# What
`aggregate_rebuild`: the choke point that turns a batch's runs and scores into folded cell aggregates. Reference Part 3 §2.9; spec §6.1 to §6.4.

# Steps (exact order)
1. Claim the lease for (aggregate_rebuild, batch_id) (keyed by batch).
2. runs = list by batch. None -> log, zero output, success (still chains).
3. scores = list by batch ordered (run_id, grader_idx, dimension), grouped per run into grader entries {idx, dims widened from f32, detail from the grader's first row}.
4. Per run: load the task (cached; error -> job error); run quality with dimension weights (error -> `task %s dimension_weights: %w`), the overlay for high-stakes, f32 pass threshold, autofail over each grader's detail.
5. Cell = (column, capability, tier); the cell's matrix_version is from the first run seen. Append run stats (pass, latency if non-null, cost if decodable).
6. Per (task, column) pair: collect gradable q and shared-dimension spreads.
7. Cells sorted by (column, capability, tier); pairs by (task, column). Task outcome = ambiguity penalty(variance penalty(q).score, ambiguity(spreads)); gradable = at least one q.
8. Fold observations with AsOf = night, matrix_version, alpha, min_nights. Re-folding a night is idempotent (the same night replaces, n does not double count).
9. On success enqueue `regression_scan` then `calibration_score` with {night, batch_id}. Go used the job context for this (QUIRK J12) and wrote a critical `job_failure` alert per failed enqueue (message `aggregate_rebuild %s could not enqueue %s for batch %s: %v`). In Rust, enqueue them in the same transaction as the completion (D11) so they cannot be lost.

# Divergences
D6: add the `availability` dimension (fraction of scheduled repeats that returned output, errors and timeouts included in the denominator) and exclude error runs from quality. D7: latency percentiles include timeouts censored at the timeout value (the timeout is the runner's per-run timeout). Tag tests.

# Parity gate
Bit-exact float32 fixtures: `ewma.json#fold_observations_via_float32_storage/*`, `observe.json`; DB tests TestFoldObservationsThreeNights (values within 1e-5 and bit-exact f32), TestFoldObservationsMultipleDimensions, TestSaveScoresRoundTrip; the property tests (run quality bounds, penalty properties, shared-dimension spread bounds, variance sigma formula within 1e-12, EWMA bounds, resume matches direct fold).

# Done when
Rows pass bit-exact where required. Commit.

title: Implement regression_scan with dedup, severity by tenant bar, and the parse-failure watch
description:
# What
`regression_scan` with the parse-failure watch. Reference Part 3 §2.10; spec §6.5, §11; domain math from the regression bead.

# Steps
1. Cells = every `quality` aggregate row with `as_of = night` (ALL cells folded that night, not only this batch's; QUIRK J4, so on Sundays the second scan is a no-op through dedup).
2. Per cell: series = quality rows with as_of <= night (widened f32); detect regressions; keep findings with AsOf == night.
3. Dedup state: existing `regression` alerts for the cell (subject match on model_column_id, capability, difficulty_tier compared as TEXT), ordered (created_at, id); state = latest as_of (ties keep the earlier row). Filter: alert again only after 7 days or if 2 points deeper.
4. Severity: pools containing the column (ordered tenant_id, name), each tenant once; bar = tenant_weights.quality_bar for the capability (widened f32) else 0.80; critical if the drop crosses any tenant's bar, else warning.
5. Alert subject keys: `as_of, baseline, batch_id, capability, current, delta, difficulty_tier, dimension, model_column_id, regression_kind` (`drop` | `shock`). The first five are the history-marker contract. Message exact with U+2192 arrow and U+2212 minus: `quality regression (%s) on %s %s tier %d: %.1f → %.1f (−%.1f pts) as of %s`.

# Parse-failure watch
Batch rate per column (runs of this batch), trailing rate over runs with ran_at in [nightStart - 7 days, nightStart) (QUIRK J5: wall clock), already-alerted columns for this night. Alert iff rate > 0.05 AND rate > 2.0 x trailing (both strict). Kind `parse_failure_rate`, warning, subject keys `batch_id, model_column_id, night, parse_failure_rate, parse_failures, total_runs, trailing_rate`, message exact with U+00D7.

# Output
`{batch_id, cells_scanned, regression_alerts, parse_failure_alerts}`. Claim the lease keyed by batch; re-running a night is a no-op.

# Parity gate
`regression.json` (DB-backed cases) and reference Part 3 §6 regression_scan tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement prediction_lock and calibration_score
description:
# What
`prediction_lock` (02:50) and `calibration_score` (chained after rebuild). Reference Part 3 §2.8, §2.11, §3; master plan §3.1 "Calibration".

# prediction_lock
1. Active corpus, active tasks, runnable columns.
2. Scheduled cells = {(column, capability, tier)} for smoke x non-cold plus all x cold_start; if `cronFiresOn(MAVERICK_CRON_WEEKLY, night)` also all x all runnable (`sweep_night: true`).
3. Latest `pass_rate` aggregate per cell (any date; QUIRK J11: if tonight's rebuild already exists, that row is used).
4. Derive: cells without an EWMA are skipped; p = clamp(ewma, 0, 1); sorted by (column, capability, tier); each once.
5. Insert with `batch_id = the NIGHT tag` (not a runner batch id), `predicted_pass_prob = f32(p)`, `source = "ewma"`, `matrix_version = active corpus`, `locked_at = now`; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (first lock wins).
Output `{night, sweep_night, scheduled_cells, locked_cells, inserted_rows}`.
Why: locking before results makes hindsight impossible; the `source` column lets later predictors (matrix completion, IRT) compete on the same ledger.

# calibration_score
1. Locked predictions for the night tag; none -> warn, `skipped: true`.
2. Runs of the batch; none -> skipped.
3. Per run: run quality (same choke point as rebuild); p = locked prob for its cell; missing -> `unlocked_runs++`; else append {p, pass} under the capability.
4. Per capability (sorted): upsert calibration (batch_id = the REAL batch id, capability, brier f32, overconfidence f32, n); conflict updates values and scored_at.
Output `{batch_id, locked_cells, pairs, unlocked_runs, calibration_rows, skipped?}`.

# Parity gate
`predictions.json` DB-backed cases and reference Part 3 §6 predictions and jobs tests. Lease-claim both handlers (prediction_lock by night; calibration by batch).

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement latency_probes for secondary-endpoint columns
description:
# What
`latency_probes` (hourly): thin pings for secondary-endpoint columns, feeding their latency cells only. Reference Part 3 §2.12; spec §11; master plan §3.1 ("quality is a property of the model, latency and price are properties of the path to it").

# Rules (exact)
- Probe prompt: the 60-character string `Reply with the single word pong to this latency probe line. ` (trailing space) repeated 67 times (4020 chars). max_tokens 100, temperature 0, settings = column settings (none when empty). 5 sequential pings per column.
- Columns: runnable (by id) with `quality_source_column_id` set. Source cells = latest `quality` and `pass_rate` aggregates of the SOURCE column, one per (capability, tier), first row in query order (pass_rate sorts first, so its matrix_version wins). No measured check (QUIRK J6). No source cells -> skip without probing.
- Missing client or bad settings -> 5 failures, no pings. Each ping timeout = `MAVERICK_RUNNER_TIMEOUT`. Latency = elapsed ms (truncated) of successful calls. A cancelled job stops early without counting remaining pings.
- At least one success: `{latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms}` by nearest rank over sorted successes; fold into each source cell ON THE PROBE COLUMN with AsOf = UTC date of the `hour` arg and the source row's matrix_version. Later passes on the same day replace the day's row (n increments once per day).
- Output `{columns, probes_ok, probes_failed, cells_updated}`.
- These calls use operator keys (benchmark use); in CI only the fake provider.

# Parity gate
Reference Part 3 §6 latency_probes tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement price_sync and catalog_sync (lifecycle, retirement guard, drift check, retention_expiring)
description:
# What
`price_sync` (06:00) and `catalog_sync` (06:10). Reference Part 3 §2.13 and §5; spec §4.1 to §4.5, §7.2, §11.

# price_sync
1. No price source configured -> info log, zero output (Go behavior; still valid). Define the price-source trait here; the models.dev implementation (owner decision 2026-09-28) is bead 7.15.
2. Source error -> job error.
3. Per runnable column (by id): look up (provider, model_id, endpoint); missing -> count; equal input/output/currency -> skip (as_of and source not compared); else snapshot JSON `{"input_per_mtok","output_per_mtok","currency","as_of","source"}` (as_of defaults to the job day), update the column preserving every other field, log `catalog_changes` change=pricing. Historical `runs.cost` is NEVER restated.
Output `{columns, updated, missing_from_source}`.

# catalog_sync
1. measured = columns with any `measured = true` aggregate.
2. cold_start columns: activate when `cold_start_until` is set, day >= it, and measured.
3. deprecated columns: when `deprecation_date` <= day, run the retirement guard; blocked -> count and warn (the guard already wrote the critical alert; QUIRK J8: it re-alerts every day); allowed -> `retired`.
4. Drift check: every pool whose G4 survivors <= 1 -> `pool_would_be_empty`, critical at 0 (`has no usable columns`), warning at 1 (`is within one column of empty`); subject keys and message exact (Go `%q` quoting of the pool name). No dedup (J8). The drift simulation includes zero retention (D1).
5. NEW (spec §4.5): `retention_expiring` warning 14 days before any column's or alias's `retention_valid_until`. Expired evidence reads as `unknown` everywhere, which can empty a zero-retention pool; the drift check must catch it.
6. Status changes log `catalog_changes` change=status.
Output `{activated, retired, retirement_blocked, drift_alerts}` plus a retention counter.

# Parity gate
`catalog.json` DB-backed cases and reference Part 3 §6 catalog tests; new retention tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Build the sdk-conformance mock engine and mock provider servers with a language-neutral control API
description:
# What
The `sdk-conformance` crate's servers: a mock MM engine and a mock provider that run scripted scenarios, as a binary that SDK repos (TypeScript, Ruby, Go, Python) start in their CI. `plans/model-maverick-sdk-v0-plan.md` §2.3; master plan §3.5, §7.2 N2.

# Mock engine
- `POST /v1/recommend`: scripted responses per scenario (declared and prompt forms; chains with `settings`, `retention_mode`, `execution_aliases`; `zero_retention` flag; the terminal errors `422 zero_retention_requires_declared` and `409 no_compliant_columns`; outage by refusing connections or 5xx).
- `POST /v1/telemetry`: records every batch byte for byte so scenarios can assert shape, timing, and "zero bytes when off".
- Records every recommend request (form, projection version, headers) for assertions.

# Mock provider
Scripted per scenario: 2xx, 429 with `Retry-After`, 500, timeout (slow headers), connection refused, 400/422 semantic errors, SSE streams. Speaks the OpenAI chat-completions and Anthropic Messages shapes, plus an OpenRouter-like endpoint for the openrouter mode.

# Control interface
A small control API or CLI (`sdk-conformance serve --scenario <name>` or a control endpoint to load a scenario and read results) so a test in any language can drive it. Keep it language-neutral: HTTP + JSON only. Document it in the crate README.

# Rules
No provider schema translation anywhere. No real network. Deterministic.

# Done when
Both mock servers run from the binary and a Rust smoke test drives one scenario through them. Commit.

title: Freeze the conformance scenarios and JSON test vectors (incl. zero-retention and OpenRouter cases)
description:
# What
The frozen cross-language scenarios and JSON test vectors. sdk-v0 plan §2.3 ("twelve frozen scenarios"; the plan enumerates nine numbered groups, some with sub-cases; freeze the list with stable ids and record the mapping); openrouter spec (conformance additions); master plan §3.5, §3.6.

# Scenarios (enumerated once, frozen as the contract)
1. Declared-form happy path; prompt-form happy path.
2. Provider 429 with `Retry-After` -> chain advances after the wait.
3. Provider 500 / timeout / connection refused -> chain advances.
4. Provider 400/422 -> no advance, error surfaced verbatim.
5. Chain exhausted -> last provider error surfaced.
6. MM down -> cached chain used; cold cache -> default model; `privacy: off` -> MM never contacted. Zero-retention: (a) engine answers 422 `zero_retention_requires_declared` or 409 `no_compliant_columns` -> error surfaced, no fail-open, cached chains for the tenant purged; (b) warm-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> only `zero`-stamped entries used; (c) cold-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> fail closed unless the default model is locally marked verified zero-retention.
7. Telemetry: batch shape, interval flush, exit flush, silent drop on failure; `check_pass` absent when no check ran (never defaulted to true); `settings_applied` set when entry settings were applied.
8. `MODELMAVERICK_TELEMETRY=off` -> zero bytes to `/v1/telemetry` (asserted by the mock).
9. Alias parsing table, including pass-through of concrete model names and the `?settings=caller` suffix (entry settings applied by default, left alone with the suffix). The prompt-form request carries the workload projection and its version; an `X-Maverick-Workload` override sends the declared form.
Plus (openrouter spec): a zero-retention tenant with an OpenRouter key: ZDR option on every attempt, unverified aliases skipped, 409 when none remain, no direct-key fallback; alias-less chain -> no_executable_candidates.

# Test vectors
JSON files for: alias parsing table (shared with the Rust alias bead), workload projection inputs and exact outputs (shared with the projection bead), telemetry item derivation, retention expiry evaluation. Version the vector set.

# Done when
Scenarios and vectors are committed with stable ids and a README describing how an SDK runs them. Commit.

title: Full-stack e2e test script: migrate, seam, corpus, batch chain, recommend, proxy, MCP, privacy checks, with step logs
description:
# What
A full-stack end-to-end test script that exercises the real binaries together, with detailed step logging, and runs in CI with no real providers. It proves the pieces that each package tested alone actually work as one system.

# Script (`scripts/e2e.sh` or an `xtask e2e`, plus a cargo integration test that wraps it)
1. Start Postgres 16 (testcontainers or a docker run), print its URL.
2. `maverick migrate`; assert exit 0.
3. Start the fake-provider HTTP server (scripted responses for the mini-corpus prompts, judge, and classifier) and point every provider base URL at it through engine config.
4. `maverick serve --worker-only` and `maverick serve --api-only` as separate processes (the real deploy shape); wait for `/up`.
5. Through the internal seam: create columns (two providers, one secondary endpoint), create a tenant, issue an API key, set pools/weights/constraints, set a zero-retention tenant with a ZR column.
6. `maverick corpus load` + `activate` with `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/e2e_corpus/`.
7. Enqueue `prediction_lock` and `nightly_smoke` for a fixed night (via an operator trigger or the job client); wait for `aggregate_rebuild`, `regression_scan`, `calibration_score` to finish; assert `batches` rows are completed exactly once.
8. `POST /v1/recommend` (declared and prompt forms); assert pick, chain, flags, trace row, `measured` as expected for one night.
9. Start `maverick-proxy` in self-hosted and hosted modes against the engine and the fake providers; send one chat and one messages request each; assert relay, correlation headers, telemetry arrives in `outcomes`.
10. Privacy spot checks: zero-retention tenant prompt form without a ZR classifier -> 422; canary string in a request appears in no process log.
11. MCP: `tools/list` and one `recommend_model` over `/mcp`.
12. Shut everything down with SIGTERM; assert clean exits and drained alerts.

# Logging
Every step prints a numbered header, the command or request, status, elapsed time, and on failure the last 200 lines of each process log (engine logs are JSON; pretty-print them). Artifacts (process logs, captured requests) go to `target/e2e/<timestamp>/` for CI upload.

# Rules
No real provider, no network beyond localhost, no corpus content (synthetic mini-corpus only). Deterministic: fixed night, fixed clock where the engine allows it.

# Done when
The script passes locally and in CI, and a deliberately broken step produces a readable failure report. Commit.

title: Build the Docker images, Kamal 2 config (engine + hosted proxy), and backup/restore scripts
description:
# What
The deploy images and the Kamal 2 config for the Rust engine and the hosted trial proxy. Master plan §4 "Deployment"; spec §14.2; `config/deploy-go-reference.yml` (Go config, reference only). This bead needs NO owner input: the host is only needed to deploy (go-live bead).

# Images
Multi-stage Docker with cargo-chef for cached dependency layers, a static musl binary, a distroless static final image, rustls only (no OpenSSL). One image for `maverick` (three process shapes via args: `serve`, `serve --api-only`, `serve --worker-only`), one for `maverick-proxy`.

# Kamal 2 config (host values are placeholders until the owner supplies the host)
- Engine service: `serve` (or `--api-only` replicas plus exactly one `--worker-only`); health check `GET /up`; migrations in a pre-boot hook (`maverick migrate`); the internal listener (:8081) never routed through the Kamal proxy, private network only.
- Postgres 16 as an accessory with a named volume.
- Hosted trial proxy service (owner decision 2026-09-28): hosted mode, public route, NO provider env keys in its environment (D12), tenant keys via `X-Maverick-API-Key`, per-tenant rate limits (D28), reaches the engine's public listener.
- Secrets: `MAVERICK_DATABASE_URL`, `MAVERICK_INTERNAL_TOKENS`, capture master keys, operator provider keys (engine only), SMTP and webhook settings.
- Backups: a nightly `pg_dump` to an off-box target (target URL and credentials are secrets supplied at deploy time) plus a scripted restore test that restores into a scratch database and runs `maverick migrate` and a row-count check. title: Write and execute the go-live runbook (fresh install, engine + hosted proxy)
description:
# What
Go-live: the Rust engine and the hosted trial proxy start serving on the deploy host. Master plan §7.0 step 4. The Go implementation was never shipped, and the owner chose a FRESH database (bead 10.4), so this is a clean install, not a cutover: no backup of Go data, no adopt command, no `batches` backfill, no River tables.

# Runbook (write it as `docs/runbook-go-live.md` first; then execute it with the owner)
1. Provision secrets on the host: `MAVERICK_DATABASE_URL`, `MAVERICK_INTERNAL_TOKENS`, capture master key and version, provider keys (operator keys, for benchmarks and classification only), SMTP and webhook settings, spend caps, classifier limits (placeholders 1000/day per tenant, $5/day global).
2. Deploy Postgres 16 (Kamal accessory, named volume) and confirm the nightly off-box backup and its restore test work.
3. Deploy the engine image; the pre-boot hook runs `maverick migrate` (sqlx + graphile_worker schema). Check `/up` and `/health/detail` (`job_queue` shows the worker).
4. Through the internal seam (private network only): create the catalog columns for the four launch providers, with pricing and retention evidence; set execution aliases and parameter constraints where known.
5. Clone `donnfelker/model-maverick-corpus` on the host (outside any repo checkout), then `maverick corpus load --version <v> --dir <path>/corpus` and `maverick corpus activate --version <v>`. Expect 221 tasks, no warnings.

7. Deploy the hosted trial proxy (hosted mode: no provider env keys, per-tenant rate limits). Smoke test: one chat and one messages request through the hosted proxy with the tenant key and a caller-supplied provider key.
8. Confirm the nightly schedule: `prediction_lock` 02:50, `nightly_smoke` 03:00 UTC.
Rollback: restore the (young) database backup and fix forward in Rust.

Needs the deploy host and Kamal access (bead 10.3) and provider keys (bead 10.2). Every production step is outward-facing: confirm each one with the owner before running it. Never touch the firewall of the development VPS.

# Done when
Rust serves on the host, the hosted proxy answers, the runbook is committed, and the cutover is recorded in the close reason.

title: Build the pre-registered distribution-check tool for the first live nightly vs Go-era aggregates
description:
# What
Write the pre-registered distribution-check tool BEFORE the first live Rust nightly (master plan §7.0 success criterion). Only needed if the owner keeps the Go-era database, but cheap to build either way.

# Tool
A `maverick` subcommand or `xtask` that reads the Go-era aggregates and the first Rust nightly's aggregates from the same database and reports:
- Mean paired delta per provider and per capability, with the pooled standard error, pass/fail.
- The fraction of cells outside max(2 sigma, 2 points) with variance floored at 2 points (the variance comes from `aggregates.variance`), pass iff <= 5%.
- Regression alerts raised by the first Rust nightly, for manual attribution.
- Actual spend vs projected spend, pass iff within 10%.
Freeze the thresholds in code and commit before the run (that is what "pre-registered" means).

The tool runs against a test database seeded with synthetic Go-era and Rust rows and produces the report. Commit.
